result.angle:
BASEBALL REALISM FIRST. Every bar maps to something a manager actually watches. Health (HP) is how well he is holding up today, meaning his command and composure. It works like a live Game Score: walks, hits and runs drain it, and outs, clean innings and mound visits refill it. Fatigue (ARM) is section 5's pitch budget made visible. It drains pitch by pitch, and long or high-stress innings drain it faster. "Fainting" is the Pokemon name for being forced out of the game: KNOCKED OUT (HP 0, shelled and chased), OUT OF GAS (ARM 0, no manager leaves him in) or INJURED (struck by a comebacker). The bars react only to what already happened. They never change a play's result. They only change how he pitches from then on and when he has to leave. Every substitution follows MLB rules: no re-entry, the reliever inherits the count and the runners, inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on, the 3-batter minimum applies (with its injury exemption), and a position player pitches if the bullpen is empty. Batters never faint. Their bar is still the count.

Note to paste into the brief as a new section 4b ("Pitcher Health, Fatigue and fainting"). It replaces the section 4 line "the pitcher's bar is stamina":
"It's still baseball. Every pitch and play resolves exactly as in section 4. A hit is a hit, an out is an out, and runs, outs, innings and the final score are pure baseball. The Pokemon layer sits on the pitcher only. He has two bars. HEALTH (HP) is his command and composure today: walks, hits and runs drain it, and outs, shutdown innings and mound visits refill a little. FATIGUE (ARM) is his pitch budget: every pitch drains it, and nothing refills it during a game. If either bar reaches zero, the pitcher faints. He is knocked out of the game (HP) or out of gas (ARM) and must be replaced, the way a real manager would have to. Low bars make his future pitches worse, never plays already made. Batters don't faint; their bar is still the count. Fainting follows MLB substitution rules: no re-entry, the reliever inherits the count and the runners, inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on, the three-batter minimum applies except for injury, and a position player pitches if the bullpen is empty."
result.health_bar:
WHAT IT IS (baseball terms): how well he is holding up today, meaning his command, composure and the manager's patience. It is modeled on Tango's Game Score v2 (outs and strikeouts add, hits, walks, runs and homers subtract), which fans already accept as "how good was this outing". It is NOT a talent rating. Talent shows up in how rarely he takes damage.

SIZE: HP_max = 100 for every pitcher, every appearance, starter or reliever. A new pitcher always enters at 100. Health resets every game. Formula after each event: HP = min(100, HP - damage + recovery).

DAMAGE (applied to the pitcher on the mound after the play is final; all values are config constants and these are the starting values):
- Walk 4, HBP 4 (an intentional walk, if ever added: 0, because it is the manager's choice)
- Single 5, Double 7, Triple 8, Home run 10 (harder results hurt more, the Pokemon "critical" feel, but always decided by the result type, never re-rolled)
- Each run that scores while he is pitching: 8, including inherited runners (it happened on his watch; the official charge still follows MLB rules, see faint_rules). It is 4 if the run is error-tainted: the runner reached on an error, or the run scored on an error or passed ball.
- Batter reaches on error: 2 (extra traffic)
- Wild pitch: 2 (plus any runs). Passed ball: 0 (catcher's fault).
- Stolen base or caught stealing: 0
- Comebacker strikes the pitcher: 25 + random 0-25 (see faint_rules for injury). Only possible on grounders or liners whose already-resolved result is a single or an infield out, so the narration ("deflects off Smith to the shortstop") fits the result.

RECOVERY:
- Each out recorded: +1 (any out, including sac bunts and sac flies)
- Strikeout: +2 instead of +1 ("strikeouts get you out of jams")
- Double play: +2 bonus on top of the two outs (+4 total). Triple play: +3 bonus.
- Finishing a half-inning: +4 (regroup in the dugout, a word with the pitching coach). Another +6 if no runs scored while he was pitching that half (a shutdown inning, "he's settling in"). The bonus counts even if he entered mid-inning.
- Mound visit: +15, plus 5 pitches of Steadied (see performance_effects)
- Never above 100.

WORKED NUMBERS (use them as unit-test fixtures):
- League-average inning (4.3 PA, 0.48 R): about 11 damage and about 12 recovery. An average pitcher hovers near full, and Health only moves when trouble clusters, just like a real manager's leash.
- 4-run inning (1B, 1B, BB, 2B, 2-run HR, 3 outs): 31 hit/walk damage + 32 run damage - 3 - 4 = net -56, leaving 44 (Rattled).
- 6-run inning: about 20 HP mid-inning, which triggers the AI hook. 8 runs in one inning means KNOCKED OUT.
- Slow bleed (2, 1, 2, 1 runs over four innings): a 2-run inning costs a net 30, a 1-run inning a net 13, leaving 14 HP (On the ropes). One more run and he faints.
- Settling in: 4 runs in the 1st (44 HP), then four 1-hit scoreless innings at +8 each brings him back to 76.
result.fatigue_bar:
WHAT IT IS: section 5's pitch budget, shown on screen. It REPLACES section 4's "stamina HP bar" and any separate fatigue logic in section 5. It is one system, not two.

BUDGET B: his real average pitches per appearance (blended 2026 weight 1, 2025 weight 0.5, per section 3). Pitchers with 5+ starts use pitches per start; everyone else uses pitches per relief appearance. Clamped to 12-105. The Stamina rating is the readable layer on B.

TANK T (the bar's full size): T = B + max(8, round(0.30 x B)). Examples: B=88 starter gives T=114. B=17 one-inning reliever gives T=25. B=30 long man gives T=39. The stretch between B and T is the "running on fumes" zone, which matches real ceilings of about 110-120 pitches for starters and 25-30 for relievers.

DRAIN: ARM = T - U, where U is accumulated cost. Cost per pitch:
- base 0.90
- +0.20 if any runner is on base (working from the stretch with traffic)
- +0.40 if it is his 21st or later pitch of the current inning (the laborious inning that really tires a pitcher)
- Pickoff throws, if added later: 0.5
Calibrate so the league-average cost per pitch is 1.00 +/- 0.03. That keeps B meaning "pitches": clean, quick innings cost slightly less than their pitch count, and grinding innings cost more.

NO RECOVERY in-game. Sitting in the dugout doesn't rest an arm, and a mound visit doesn't either (a visit restores Health, not the arm). That is realistic and is the key difference between the two bars.

Example (B=88, T=114): "tiring" (yellow) at U >= 70 (0.8B). Past budget (red) at 88, where penalties begin exactly as section 5 says. Faint at 114.

SEASON MODE CARRYOVER (Health always starts at 100):
- A reliever who pitched in the previous game starts with U0 = 0.5 x yesterday's U, capped so ARM starts at 50% or more.
- A reliever who pitched in each of the last two games is unavailable to the AI. The human gets a warning, and he starts at 50%.
- A reliever who fainted from ARM is unavailable the next game.
- Starters on normal rotation are always fresh.
- An INJURED faint costs 1-5 games (random), shown on the roster screen.
result.performance_effects:
Rule: modifiers apply only to pitches not yet thrown. A play already resolved is never revisited. Health affects COMMAND only (a rattled pitcher overthrows and misses spots, but his stuff doesn't vanish). Fatigue affects command, velocity, stuff and contact quality (a tired arm loses everything). Effects multiply together. Clamp every probability to [0.02, 0.95].

FATIGUE: overage O = clamp((U - B) / (T - B), 0, 1). While U < B, O = 0 and there is NO effect (unchanged from section 5).
Past budget:
- Velocity: -3.0 mph x O on every pitch, shown in the pitch menu ("94 -> 92").
- Step 1 (ball or strike): P(ball) x (1 + 0.20 x O). Mistake rate (the pitch leaks over the heart of the plate, missing the chosen location) +6 percentage points x O.
- Step 3 (contact or whiff): every pitch's whiff rate x (1 - 0.25 x O).
- Step 5 (ball in play): HR per ball in play allowed x (1 + 0.40 x O). BABIP allowed + 0.030 x O.
- Wild pitch chance x (1 + 0.5 x O).
Intended size: opponents' OPS about +.050 at O=0.5 and about +.120 near O=1. That is enough that riding a gassed pitcher visibly backfires, which is realistic.

HEALTH tiers:
- 51-100 Composed: no effect.
- 21-50 Rattled: P(ball) x 1.06, mistake rate +3 percentage points, wild pitch x 1.25.
- 1-20 On the ropes: P(ball) x 1.12, mistake rate +6 percentage points, wild pitch x 1.5.
- Health never touches whiff rates, velocity, or batted-ball quality directly. Mistakes produce harder contact through the existing location logic ("mistakes go deep").

STEADIED (the next 5 pitches after a mound visit): Health tier penalties are suspended and P(ball) x 0.95. This is the brief's "steadies control for a few pitches". It does not offset fatigue.

RUSHED (a reliever forced in by a sudden faint, see faint_rules): P(ball) x 1.10 for his first batter only.

Calibration rule: all section 6 targets are tuned with these effects ON. Bars are not something you switch on after calibrating.
result.faint_rules:
WHAT A FAINT IS: forced removal from the game. There are three causes:
- KNOCKED OUT: HP reaches 0 (he's been shelled; the manager has to take the ball).
- OUT OF GAS: ARM reaches 0 (no manager leaves him in past this; it would risk his arm).
- INJURED: a comebacker strikes the pitcher; of those, 20% are injuries, and HP is set to 0 with an injury flag.
These numbers give a pitcher struck in about 2% of team-games and an injury exit in about 0.4%.

EXACT ORDER AFTER EVERY PITCH (engine, DOM-free):
1. Resolve the pitch and everything it causes: ball or strike, contact, batted-ball result, every runner advance, outs, runs, WP/PB.
2. Record the play in the game state and box score. It is now final and immutable.
3. If the plate appearance ended, add 1 to his batters faced in this appearance.
4. Apply the ARM cost for the pitch, and HP damage and recovery for the events.
5. Apply the floors: the 3-batter rule and the last-arm rule.
6. Faint check: is HP <= 0 or ARM <= 0?
7. If the half-inning ended and he is still in, apply the inning-end recovery.
The faint check comes before the inning-end recovery, so a dugout regroup can't save a pitcher who was already at 0.

WHEN THE FAINT LANDS:
- On a pitch that ended the plate appearance: the next batter faces the reliever, starting at 0-0.
- Mid at-bat (ball, strike, foul, or a WP/PB that didn't end the PA): the plate appearance stays live. The reliever inherits the exact count, the same batter, the outs and the runners. Charging follows MLB Rule 9.16(h). If the count was 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2 when he left AND the batter walks, the walk and that batter (as a runner) go to the departed pitcher. Any other result (hit, out, strikeout, HBP, error, fielder's choice), and every result from any other count, goes to the reliever.
- On the pitch that ends the half-inning: nobody enters mid-inning. He simply doesn't come back out, and the reliever starts the next half.

INHERITED RUNNERS (Rule 9.16(g)): they stay charged to the pitcher who put them on. If they score, R and ER go to him, and the reliever's line logs IR/IRS. The reliever's HP still takes 8 for that run, because the bars track what happened on the mound and the box score follows the rulebook.

REPLACEMENT ENTERS at HP 100 and full ARM (less any Season carryover).
RUSHED: applies when the faint was KO or GAS and, at the start of that plate appearance, the departed pitcher had HP > 50 and U < B. Nobody would have been warming up, so the reliever is Rushed for his first batter (P(ball) x 1.10). No Rushed status after an injury (MLB lets an injured pitcher's replacement take as many warmup pitches as he needs) or after a voluntary change.

3-BATTER MINIMUM (Rule 5.10(g)): a pitcher may leave only if (a) he has completed 3 batters in this appearance (each one retired or reached base), or (b) a half-inning has just ended, or (c) he is INJURED.
- Until then, non-injury damage and drain cannot take HP or ARM below 1. Text: "He's hanging on!", like the Pokemon Sturdy ability.
- The voluntary BULLPEN command is disabled, with the reason shown.
- Step 3 runs before step 4, so the 3rd batter's result counts: his hit can KO the pitcher, and once that batter's PA ends, the pitcher is fair game.
- A pitcher held at 1 stays at 1 until his next damaging event. Being at 1 is not a faint.
- An injury bypasses the minimum immediately, even mid at-bat.

RE-ENTRY: a removed pitcher (fainted or pulled) can never re-enter this game (Rule 5.10(d)). The engine rejects it, and the UI shows him greyed out as FNT or USED. He doesn't move to a fielding position (this avoids the DH-loss rules).

EMPTY BULLPEN, in order:
1. Any unused pitcher on the game roster.
2. An unused bench position player, using a fixed position-player pitching profile (see editor_and_data). The human may also choose one voluntarily, but only in extra innings, when trailing by 8+ or when leading by 10+ (the MLB position-player pitching rule). In an emergency, he can come in at any score.
3. If no one is left: LAST ARM. The current pitcher's HP and ARM floor at 1 and he keeps pitching at maximum penalties ("No one left in the pen!"). This also applies to the vanishingly rare case of an injury with nobody left, which is logged. Extra innings start with a runner on second, so these games still end.

SCORING: a faint never edits any recorded result. W/L/SV/holds, ER and pitch counts follow MLB rules exactly as they would without bars. A fainted pitcher keeps his line and can still be the pitcher of record. The exit reason is metadata only.
result.ai_and_player:
RULES ARE IDENTICAL AT EVERY DIFFICULTY (they are baseball). Difficulty changes only how smart the opposing manager is and how much the game helps the human.

AI MANAGER HOOK (checked between batters and at the start of each half-inning, always subject to the 3-batter rule; mid at-bat changes happen only through faints):
- ARM: at the start of an inning, don't send him back out if U >= B - 6. Mid-inning, pull if U >= B with a runner in scoring position, or if U >= B + 0.35(T - B).
- HP: pull at HP <= 20 any time, or HP <= 35 with a runner on base.
- The existing section 5 logic still applies: platoon matchups, closer in save spots, and skipping relievers whose ARM is under 50% (Season).
- VISIT: the AI visits the first time its pitcher drops into Rattled with a runner in scoring position, if visits remain and it isn't about to pull him.
- After a faint, it picks the reliever with the same section 5 logic.
- Goal: AI-run pitchers almost never faint from fatigue, and only occasionally from health after a sudden blowup. That matches a real manager's hook.

DIFFICULTY:
- Rookie: the opposing AI has a slow hook (HP <= 10; U >= B + 0.6(T - B)), never visits and ignores matchups. The human gets pitching coach prompts at Rattled, at 0.8B and at budget ("Smith is tiring. Bring in Jones?" Yes/No), and damage numbers float over the bar.
- Pro: the standard hook above. Text warnings only.
- All-Star: the AI has a quick hook (HP <= 40 with runners on; U >= B - 10 at inning start), visits well, plays matchups hard, and always has someone warm, so its relievers are never Rushed. The human gets bars only, with no prompts.

WHAT THE HUMAN SEES AND DOES:
- Both pitchers' HP and ARM bars are always visible. The opponent's bars use public information: pitch count is on every scoreboard, and Health comes from hits, walks and runs everyone saw.
- BULLPEN: a list of relievers with throws, role and ARM bar (Season), with FNT/USED pitchers greyed out. During the 3-batter minimum it is disabled: "Smith must face 2 more batters (3-batter minimum)."
- VISIT: +15 HP and Steadied for 5 pitches. 2 per game. If both are used before the 6th, 1 more in the 6th (MLB's ninth-inning bonus, scaled), and +1 per extra inning (MLB). Only one visit per pitcher per inning. In MLB a second trip to the same pitcher in an inning forces his removal, so the menu says that and sends you to BULLPEN.
- AUTO (pitching coach): uses the Pro hook for the inning, including visits and changes.
- When your pitcher faints: a forced bullpen picker opens (no cancel, like Pokemon's "choose your next Pokemon"), with the coach's recommended arm highlighted. On AUTO the coach picks.

ON OFFENSE you drain the opposing pitcher's bars only by playing baseball. There is no special "attack" command.
- Work counts and spoil pitches (Take or Protect produces more fouls and longer at-bats). That runs up his pitch count and drains ARM, the real "make him throw strikes" strategy.
- String hits together to drain HP.
- AI hitters do the same: facing a pitcher past budget, they lean toward Take on 0-0 and 1-0 counts (+10% Take weight).
result.ui_and_text:
BARS ON SCREEN (pitcher info box, near and far, in Pick & Roll style):
- Two stacked bars, about 140px wide and 6px tall at 390px width.
- Top bar "HP" with "64/100" beside it.
- Bottom bar "ARM" with the real pitch count, e.g. "PC 79".
- A 1px white tick on the ARM bar marks the budget point B.
- The batter box is unchanged: the count bar (3 strikes empties it) plus ball and strike dots.

COLORS (meaningful: color = active penalty tier). Define them as CSS tokens.
- HP: green 51-100, yellow 21-50 (Rattled), red 1-20 (On the ropes).
- ARM: green while U < 0.8B, yellow from 0.8B to B (tiring, no penalty yet: plan the change), red at U >= B (past budget, penalties active).
- A red bar pulses slowly.
- A "STEADIED" chip shows for the 5 pitches after a visit. "RUSHED" shows on a rushed reliever's first batter.

ANIMATION ORDER (the result always comes first): the result line ("Line drive single to center!") plays, THEN the bars drain over 400ms. Heals tick up in green after an out or at inning end. A bar never moves before the play is narrated.
- Faint: the sprite sinks and fades (Pokemon faint), a low thud plays, and the screen dims for 200ms. The reliever's sprite slides in from the bullpen side.
- The existing home-run flash and strikeout ring are unchanged.

TEXT BOX LINES (exact, with the name substituted):
- HP crosses 50: "Smith is rattled! His command is slipping."
- HP crosses 20: "Smith is on the ropes!" (AI side adds: "Seattle has someone throwing in the pen.")
- ARM reaches 0.8B: "Smith is tiring. (70 pitches)"
- ARM passes B: "Smith is running on fumes! His fastball is down to 91."
- Shutdown inning: "Smith shut the door. He's settling in."
- Visit: "The pitching coach heads to the mound..." then "Smith takes a breath. He's steadied!"
- 3-batter floor: "Smith is hanging on! He has to face 1 more batter."
- KO: "Smith fainted!" then "He's been knocked out of the game."
- Out of gas: "Smith fainted!" then "He's out of gas. 114 pitches."

- Last arm: "No one left in the bullpen! Smith has to keep going!"

BOX SCORE (pitching line: IP H R ER BB K HR PC). The name carries an exit tag: "Smith (KO)", "Lee (GAS)", "Park (INJ)". Voluntary changes get no tag.
Notes in real box-score style:
- "Smith pitched to 2 batters in the 5th." (added whenever he left without recording an out in an inning)
- "Inherited runners-scored: Jones 2-1."
- "Pitches-strikes: Smith 94-61, Jones 17-11."
- "Exits: Smith knocked out (HP 0) in the 5th; Lee out of gas (114 pitches) in the 4th; Park injured, struck by batted ball, in the 3rd."
Play-by-play: "T5: Smith fainted (out of gas, 114 pitches) with a 2-1 count on Garcia. Jones replaces Smith."

CHART TAB: add a "Pitcher bars" card with the damage/recovery table, the tiers and the faint rules in plain words.
result.editor_and_data:
WHAT DRIVES THE BARS:
- ARM: driven by the existing Stamina rating. Stamina is the percentile mapping of real pitches per appearance across all pitchers (1st percentile about 12, 99th about 105). Editing Stamina moves B along that range, and T follows from the formula. Editor line: "Stamina 84 · 91 pitches/start -> Budget 91, Tank 118". A reliever edited to 99 becomes a starter-length arm, which is intended.
- HEALTH: NO new rating. Everyone has 100. The baseball rationale: no stable stat measures "composure" (strand rate is mostly luck), so a pitcher's resilience comes from his real Control, Movement and Stuff, which limit the walks, hits and runs that drain HP. The editor shows "Health 100 (all pitchers)" as read-only, with a tooltip.

DATA PIPELINE (build_data.py): no new sources. Split the existing "average pitches per appearance" field by role: per start when GS >= 5, otherwise per relief appearance. Use the section 3 blend. Store it as pitchesPerApp, plus the derived budget B.

POSITION-PLAYER PITCHING PROFILE (a fixed engine constant, not editable unless a player has two-way pitching data):
- One pitch: "BP fastball", 4-seam, 83 mph, whiff 6%
- BB rate about 9%, HR per batter faced about 8%, BABIP allowed .330
- B = 25, T = 33

ENGINE CONFIG: one constants object in engine.js holds every bar number: the damage and recovery table, the cost terms, T's 0.30 and min 8, the tier cutoffs, the effect multipliers, the comebacker rates, visit counts, and the AI hook thresholds per difficulty. Calibration tunes them in one place. No DOM.

SAVED STATE (written after every pitch, so a reload mid at-bat after a faint resumes exactly):
- Per pitcher in the game: hp, armUsed (U), budget B, tank T, inningPitchCount, battersFacedThisApp, steadiedPitchesLeft, visitedThisInning, rushed, status (active / removed), exitReason (KO / GAS / INJ / PULLED), exitInning, exitCount.
- Per team: visitsLeft.
- Per runner: chargedPitcherId.
- Season: last-2-games pitches per reliever and injury games remaining.

EDITOR PREVIEW (optional): add a pitcher preview line from the quick sim: "Avg outing: 5.1 IP, 84 pitches · knocked out in 6% of starts".
result.calibration_and_tests:
CALIBRATION (500+ AI vs AI games with bars and effects ON):
- The section 6 table must still pass. Tune the base engine constants with bars on; bars are not added after calibration.

New targets:
- Starter innings per 6-inning game: 4.6-5.3. Starter pitches: 75-88 (the brief says 70-90).
- Pitchers used per team per game: 2.3-3.2.
- Starts ending before 3.0 IP for non-injury reasons: 3-7%.
- Starters chased on Health (AI pull at its HP threshold, or KO): 5-10% of starts.
- AI vs AI faints: KO 0.5-3% of appearances; out of gas 0-0.5%; injured 0.2-1% of team-games.
- Mean ARM cost per pitch: 1.00 +/- 0.03.
- Mid at-bat pitching changes: 1% of plate appearances or fewer.
- AI mound visits: 0.3-1.0 per team per game.
- Effect checks (controlled sims with forced states, the same pitcher-batter pairs, so selection doesn't bias the result):
  - OPS against a pitcher at O >= 0.5 is .040-.150 higher than against the same pitcher at U < B.
  - BB% against Rattled pitchers is +0.5 to +1.5 points; against On the ropes, +1 to +3 points.
  - Velocity at O = 1 is about 3 mph lower.
- "Ride him" bot (never changes pitchers): the starter faints from ARM at a mean U close to T, and the game still completes.
- The human-like player still wins 60-65% on Pro.

HEADLESS ENGINE TESTS (seeded RNG):
1. Outcome immutability: the play result is frozen before the bar step. Replaying the play log with the bar step skipped reproduces the same results and box score for those plays.
2. Exact damage fixtures from the worked examples (4-run inning leaves 44, slow bleed leaves 14, settling in reaches 76). Recovery caps at 100.
3. ARM cost fixtures:
   - 10 pitches, bases empty, inning pitches 1-10: U = 9.0
   - the same with a runner on: U = 11.0
   - pitches 21-25 of an inning with the bases empty: 6.5
4. Threshold boundaries: at U = B, O = 0 and no effect. Just past B, the effect is active. Tier changes at HP 50/51 and 20/21.
5. Mid at-bat faint: the count, batter, runners and outs carry over.
   - 3-1 count, then a walk: charged to the departed pitcher.
   - 1-2 count, then a walk: charged to the reliever.
   - 2-strike strikeout: charged to the reliever.
6. Inherited runner: R and ER charged to the departed pitcher; the reliever's IR/IRS is correct; the reliever's HP drops by 8.
7. 3-batter rule:
   - 2 homers in a row floor him at 1.
   - The 3rd batter's single knocks him out.
   - BULLPEN is rejected before the 3rd batter, allowed between halves, and bypassed by an injury.
8. Re-entry of a removed pitcher is rejected.
9. Empty bullpen chain: bench position player, then last arm. No deadlock, and the game ends.
10. Visits: the limit of 2, the 6th-inning bonus, +1 per extra inning, and no second visit in the same inning.
11. A faint on an inning-ending pitch causes no mid-inning entry, and the reliever starts the next half.
12. Rushed is applied only in its exact conditions.
13. Save and restore at every pitch of a seeded game produces an identical continuation.
14. Season carryover and unavailability.

PLAYWRIGHT (390x844 and desktop):
- Bars render with labels, numbers and the budget tick. Using a debug hook to force states, color classes are correct at HP 45 (yellow), HP 15 (red) and U past B (red).
- A forced faint shows the text lines in order, the picker can't be dismissed, and the reliever shows the inherited count dots and runners.
- BULLPEN is disabled with a reason during the 3-batter minimum.
- Reloading right after a mid at-bat faint restores the same reliever, count, runners and score.
- A full random game through the menus: no console errors, the box score adds up, and every non-final pitcher has an exit tag or a voluntary change; the "pitched to N batters" notes are consistent.
- Screenshots added: faint text box, bullpen picker with bars, box score notes.
result.risks:
- Calibration drift: the new penalties shift league totals. Calibrate with bars on, keep the penalties small, and tune base rates first and bar constants second.
- Double-counting fatigue: ARM must replace section 5's fatigue, not stack on top of it. Delete any separate fatigue path.
- Death spiral: low HP means worse command, which means more damage. That is mitigated by command-only Health effects, the modest multipliers, visits and inning-end recovery. The controlled-sim tests catch it if the spiral is too strong.
- Health may feel static for average pitchers, because it sits near full and only blowups move it. That is realistic, but Pokemon fans may expect chip damage. The fallback is to show small floating damage numbers on Rookie, without changing the math.
- Rule complexity is bug surface: 9.16(h) walk charging, IR/IRS, ER with tainted runs, the 3-batter floor and mid at-bat swaps. The fixtures above cover it.
- The 3-batter floor ("hanging on at 1 HP") can feel unfair. The explicit text explains the rule each time.
- Exploits:
  - Visits as healing potions: capped at 2 per game and one per pitcher per inning, +15 each.
  - Riding pitchers to a faint to save the bullpen: deterred by the past-budget penalties, Rushed relievers and Season unavailability.
  - Batters stalling with Take: self-limiting, because called strikes lead to strikeouts.
- Visible opponent bars reveal when the AI's hook is coming. Acceptable, because the information is public in real baseball.
- The last-arm and position-player paths are rare and lightly exercised. Add a sim-only safety cap (e.g. 25 innings) so a headless test can't hang.
- The comebacker injury is flavor in a sensitive area. Keep it non-graphic ("the trainer helps him off").
- The 6-inning format means starters cover about 83% of innings, versus about 59% in MLB. Reliever faints will be rare, so the mechanic is mostly felt with starters.
- Mid at-bat swaps stress the UI queue and save system: sprite, count dots and charging must all survive a reload exactly at that moment.

result.angle:
POKEMON FEEL FIRST. The pitcher is the "Pokemon". He has two bars, HP (Health) and FTG (Fatigue), and the at-bat is the battle, one turn per pitch. Hits, walks and runs are the attacks that drain HP. Every pitch he throws drains FTG. When either bar is destroyed you get "COLE fainted!", which in baseball means he has been knocked out of the game or is out of gas, and you have to send someone in ("Go! CLASE!"). The batter's bar stays the count, and batters never faint.

Baseball comes first and is never touched. Each pitch and play resolves completely before the bars react: the outcome, runners, runs and outs, then the stats. After that the bars update, and then the faint check runs. Bars do only two things: they shade later pitches a little, and they force a pitcher out.

The core loop is the most satisfying part, because both halves are real baseball strategy:
- On offense you have two ways to knock out the other pitcher. DAMAGE means hitting him hard, which drains HP. GRIND means long at-bats, fouls and walks, which drains FTG ("run up his pitch count").
- On defense you face the mirror choice. Attacking the zone saves pitches (FTG) but invites contact (HP). Nibbling protects HP but burns FTG.
- Around that loop: the bars turn yellow, you get a reliever warming, you decide whether to pull him or ride him, and the faint lands like a punctuation mark. After it comes a Pokemon party-screen switch and a Shift-style "pinch-hit?" prompt.
- Faints should be common (most games have one). A Health KO should be the rarer jackpot, about 1 game in 4.

Paste-ready note for the brief (section 4): "Gameplay note: it's still baseball. Every pitch and play resolves by baseball logic first: a hit is a hit, an out is an out, and runs, outs, innings and the win are pure baseball. On top of that sits a Pokemon layer for pitchers only. An HP (Health) bar drains from hits, walks and runs, and an FTG (Fatigue) bar drains with every pitch. If either bar is destroyed, the pitcher faints (he's knocked out of the game or out of gas) and must be replaced under real MLB rules: no re-entry, the reliever inherits the count and runners, inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on, and the 3-batter minimum applies. Batters never faint; their bar is the count."
result.health_bar:
WHAT IT IS IN BASEBALL TERMS
HP is how much punishment he can take before he is "knocked out of the game" (the literal baseball phrase, along with "chased" and "KO'd"). It covers hard contact, baserunners, runs, and the odd comebacker. Think of it as a live, inverted Bill James Game Score: the things that lower a Game Score drain HP, and outs and strikeouts nudge it back up.

SIZE
- SP: HP_max = 85 + round(0.30 x Poise), giving 85 to 115 (100 at Poise 50).
- RP and CL: HP_max = 50 + round(0.20 x Poise), giving 50 to 70 (60 average). Relievers get a shorter leash.
- Position player pitching: 40.
- Rookie difficulty: the human team's pitchers get x1.15.
- Poise is a new rating (see editor_and_data). It changes only the bar size, never the pitch outcomes.

DAMAGE (applied after the play resolves, to the pitcher currently on the mound)
| Event | HP damage |
|---|---|
| Walk | 4 |
| HBP | 4 |
| Intentional walk | 0 |
| 1B | 6 |
| 2B | 9 |
| 3B | 11 |
| HR | 14 (plus run damage) |
| Batter reaches on error | 2 |
| Stolen base allowed | 1 |
| Wild pitch or balk | 2 |
| Passed ball | 0 (the catcher's fault) |
| Each run scoring while he pitches | 8 if earned, 4 if unearned (inherited runners included even though they are charged to someone else; the extra-inning placed runner is unearned, so 4) |
| Comebacker | 15 to 30, uniform; ignores Endure; physical (see faint rules) |

The comebacker is a tag on a ground ball or liner back to the mound. It is drawn after the outcome from a separate flavor RNG, about 0.25% of grounders and liners, so it never changes the play. If he survives it, he gets the HURT status.

MULTIPLIERS
- "It's super effective!": the batter sat on the correct pitch family AND got a hit. Event damage x1.5, rounded up. Run damage is not multiplied.
- "A critical hit!": a run-scoring hit with 2 outs (the two-out RBI that breaks a pitcher). Run damage for those runs x1.5.

WORKED EXAMPLES
- Bases-empty single: -6.
- Solo HR: -22. If the batter sat right: 21 + 8 = -29.
- 2-out, 3-run HR with the batter sitting right: 21 + 36 = -57.
- 2-out grand slam with the batter sitting right: 21 + 48 = -69. That knocks out a fresh 60-HP reliever, unless the 3-batter Endure rule saves him at 1.

WHAT RESTORES IT
- Each out: +1. A double play gives +2, and caught stealing or a pickoff gives +1.
- Strikeout: +2 (instead of +1).
- 1-2-3 inning: +5 at the end of the inning ("Shut-down inning!").
- VISIT, the Potion: +15 HP. It keeps the brief's control-steadying effect for 4 pitches. Limit 2 per game. It also advances a warming reliever by one batter, which is the real reason managers stall with visits.
- HP never goes above max. There is no other healing between innings, and no healing after a faint. Visits never restore FTG.

EXPECTED NUMBERS
- At league rates, damage is about 3.4 per PA and healing about 1.2 per PA, so the net is about 2.2 per PA.
- An average starter (about 20 batters faced) exits at roughly 55% HP.
- An HP KO takes something like a 5-run, 8-hit disaster. That is about 4 to 10% of starts, and about 2 to 5% of relief appearances.
result.fatigue_bar:
WHAT IT IS
Gas in the tank. It is section 5's pitch budget made visible, measured in stress-weighted pitches. A full bar means fresh; an empty bar means done. It drains in the same direction as HP, so empty always means faint. The brief's old "pitcher HP = stamina" bar becomes this FTG bar, and HP now means Health.

SIZE
- SP: FTG_max = clamp(round(1.15 x P_start), 70, 120). P_start is the blended real pitches per start. League about 88 gives 101.
- RP and CL: FTG_max = clamp(round(2.0 x P_relief), 25, 50). League about 16.5 gives 33.
- Position player: 40.
- Rookie difficulty: the human team gets x1.10.
- Stamina (the existing rating) drives P_start and P_relief.

DRAIN PER PITCH
Each pitch drains 1.0 x stress, capped at 2.0 per pitch. Stress is the product of whichever of these apply:
- Runners on, none in scoring position: x1.15 (working from the stretch, holding runners).
- Runner in scoring position: x1.30 (use this instead of x1.15).
- 7th or later pitch of the same PA: x1.20 (a long battle).
- 21st or later pitch of the same inning: x1.25 (a stressful inning).
- HURT status: x1.25.
- A pickoff throw, if modeled, costs 0.3. An automatic intentional walk costs 0.

Average stress is about 1.13. So 101 points works out to about 89 real pitches at the faint: a clean outing stretches toward about 95, a jam-filled one about 75. Combined with the AI pulling between innings, starters exit at about 75 to 86 pitches, which matches section 5's "70 to 90".

NO RECOVERY
- Pitch counts don't reset, and mound visits don't rest an arm.
- Bullpen: warming up is free. But a reliever who reaches READY and then sits down unused loses 15% of FTG_max ("got up and down twice"), and the same applies to each later re-warm.
- Season mode (optional, default on): a reliever who threw 20 or more pitches in the previous game starts at 75%. Three straight days makes him unavailable. Starters always start full.

REPLACEMENT TEXT FOR SECTION 5
"Fatigue: each pitcher's pitch budget is his Fatigue (FTG) bar, sized from his real pitches per start or appearance and drained per pitch with extra cost for runners, long at-bats and long innings. Performance fades gradually from 40% remaining (not as a cliff past the budget). At 0 he finishes the current batter on fumes and then faints. The AI manager decides from the bars."

This replaces the old "past it, velocity falls off" cliff. The budget itself now sits roughly where the bar empties. The scorebug still shows the raw pitch count; the bar is stress-weighted, so a 25-pitch jam visibly costs more than 25 clean pitches.
result.performance_effects:
ORDER OF OPERATIONS
The bars as they stand at the START of a pitch modify that pitch's probabilities. Then the play resolves. Then the bars update. Nothing is retroactive: a hit is never undone or upgraded by a bar.

FATIGUE (f = FTG / FTG_max)
- f > 0.40: no penalty, apart from the centering constant below.
- f <= 0.40: ramp p = (0.40 - f) / 0.40, from 0 up to 1. At that p:
  - Velocity -2.0p mph.
  - Whiff% x (1 - 0.12p).
  - Zone rate (Control) -5p percentage points.
  - HR per contact x (1 + 0.20p).
  - BABIP allowed +0.015p.
  - Wild-pitch rate x (1 + p).
- Amber band (16 to 40%): p up to 0.6, which is about -1.2 mph, -7% whiffs and -3 zone points.
- Red band (15% or less): p from 0.625 to 1.
- ON FUMES (FTG at 0, or at 1 under Endure, while he finishes a batter): p = 1, plus a further -1.5 mph, -3 zone points, whiff x0.92 and HR x1.10. In total that is about -3.5 mph, -8 zone points, whiff x0.81 and HR x1.32.
- Centering: a pitcher's real season rates already include his tired innings. So the engine scales the fatigue modifiers by constants chosen so that the PA-weighted mean of each modifier across Pro-vs-Pro calibration sims is 1.00 +/- 0.01. In practice, fresh pitchers play slightly better than their season line and tired ones worse, which is the real times-through-the-order shape.

HEALTH (h = HP / HP_max)
- h > 0.50: no effect.
- h <= 0.50 ("rattled"): q = (0.50 - h) / 0.50. Zone rate -3q points, and the chance of a middle-middle mistake on Attack the zone or Elevate x (1 + 0.15q).
- No effect on velocity or stuff. Being shaken is mental, not physical.
- After a VISIT, the Health penalty is suspended for 4 pitches.

STATUSES
- COLD (entered mid-inning without being READY): for his first 2 batters or 8 pitches, zone -4 points and velocity -1.0 mph.
- HURT (survived a comebacker): velocity -1.0 mph for the rest of the appearance and FTG drain x1.25.
- Caps when everything stacks: total zone penalty no more than 10 points, velocity loss no more than 5 mph, whiff multiplier no lower than x0.75.

AI HITTERS
Against a pitcher whose HP or FTG is in the red, the AI raises its Take probability by 10 points on 2-0 and 3-1 counts ("make him throw strikes"). No other change.

BATTERS
No bar effects. Their bar is the count only.
result.faint_rules:
DEFINITION
A faint is an involuntary removal from the game. There are three causes, and every one is a destroyed bar:
- KO: HP reaches 0.
- GAS: FTG reaches 0.
- INJ: HP emptied by comebacker damage.
There are no random arm injuries.

SEQUENCE EACH PITCH
1. Resolve the pitch and the play fully: outs, runners, runs, official scoring, stats.
2. Apply FTG drain and HP damage or heals.
3. Emit zone-change events.
4. Run the faint check.

WHEN THE FAINT CHECK RUNS
- Only at the end of a PA and at the end of a half-inning.
- A bar that hits 0 mid-PA does NOT remove him. FTG can hit 0 on a ball, strike or foul; HP can hit 0 from a run on a wild pitch, stolen base or balk. He gets the ON FUMES status (or ROCKED for HP), finishes the batter at full penalties, and faints the moment that PA ends, whatever the result. Baseball reason: managers don't pull a guy in the middle of a hitter unless he's hurt.
- A comebacker always ends the PA, so INJ also lands at a PA boundary.
- If the bar empties on the 3rd out, he faints walking off. The banner plays at the break, and the next inning's pitcher enters warm.
- On a game-ending play, no faint is shown; the postgame notes it.

MID-PA CHANGES AND INHERITED COUNT
- The only mid-PA change is a voluntary one by the human, allowed once the 3-batter minimum is met. The AI never changes pitchers mid-PA.
- The reliever inherits the batter, count, runners and outs.
- Walk charging follows Rule 9.16(h): if the count at the change was 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2 and the batter walks, the batter and the BB are charged to the previous pitcher. Any other result belongs to the reliever, and a strikeout is credited to the reliever.
- This change counts as a pull (OUT), not a faint.

SCORING
- A faint changes nothing in official scoring.
- Inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on (9.16(g)). Earned and unearned runs are unchanged. IP counts the outs recorded (for example 4.1). W/L/S rules are unchanged.
- HP run damage goes to whoever is on the mound when the run scores, even when the run is charged to someone else. It was his collapse.

RE-ENTRY
- Fainted and pulled pitchers can never return this game (Rule 5.10(d)).
- The party screen shows them greyed with FNT or OUT and they can't be selected.
- Unlike Pokemon: no switching back and no revives.

3-BATTER MINIMUM (Rule 5.10(g)): "ENDURE"
- A pitcher is protected until he has faced 3 batters (completed PAs) in this appearance, or the half-inning ends.
- While protected:
  - Neither bar can drop below 1 ("COLE hung on!").
  - BULLPEN is locked with the label "1 more batter".
  - No faint fires.
- Exception: comebacker damage ignores Endure and causes an immediate INJ faint. This is the rule's injury/illness exemption.
- When protection lifts at a PA end, if HP <= 1 or FTG <= 1 he faints at that same boundary. A strikeout heal can lift HP to 3, which saves him ("he settled down").
- At FTG 1 under Endure he pitches with the ON FUMES penalties.
- If he comes back out for a new inning having faced fewer than 3 batters, protection applies again until 3 total or that half-inning ends. Check this carry-over clause against the current rulebook and keep it in CONFIG.

MOUND VISITS
A second visit to the same pitcher in the same inning removes him (Rule 5.10(l)). That is a pull, not a faint.

REPLACEMENT
- The human picks on a forced party screen with no Cancel. The AI picks by its own logic.
- The reliever enters warm if he was READY, if the change is between innings, or if it follows an INJ (umpires allow unlimited warm-ups).
- Otherwise he enters COLD.

EMPTY BULLPEN
- Game staff is the SP plus 5 RP, including the CL. Other rotation starters are resting.
- If a faint leaves no pitcher, an unused bench player pitches. If there is none, the DH moves to the mound: the DH is terminated and he keeps batting in his spot.
- Emergency profile: two pitches, a 70 mph "fastball" (Stuff 5) and a 52 mph eephus (Stuff 15). Control 30, Movement 25, HP 40, FTG 40.
- Last-arm rule: a position player pitching can't faint. His bars floor at 1 and he finishes the game.
- MLB's score limit on position players pitching is waived only in this emergency.
- Target: under 0.3% of team-games.
result.ai_and_player:
WHAT THE HUMAN SEES
- Your own pitcher: HP and FTG with numbers, plus status pills.
- The opposing pitcher: bars only, with no numbers, exactly like Pokemon's enemy HP box. Rookie difficulty shows the numbers.
- The scorebug keeps the real pitch count.

HUMAN COMMANDS ON DEFENSE
- PITCH: unchanged.
- BULLPEN opens the party screen. Each reliever shows:
  - HP and FTG bars, L/R and role.
  - A tag: READY, WARMING, COLD, FNT or OUT.
  - His platoon edge against the next 3 batters, which matters because of the 3-batter rule.
  - Two actions: WARM UP (up to 2 at once; READY after 2 completed PAs or 10 pitches) and SEND IN.
- VISIT: +15 HP, steadies control for 4 pitches, and advances warm-up by one batter. 2 per game. Before a second same-inning visit to the same pitcher it warns "This visit will remove him."
- AUTO: the pitching coach calls pitches and handles every change, forced or voluntary, using Pro logic. The text reads "Coach sent out CLASE."
- Hints:
  - FTG turns amber with nobody warming: "Get someone loose in the BULLPEN?"
  - FTG red: "He's almost out of gas."

HUMAN ON OFFENSE
- The approaches are unchanged, but now there is a visible reason to grind.
- When the opposing pitcher's FTG turns amber: "He's tiring. Make him work."
- Shift prompt: after ANY opponent pitching change, including a faint, the game asks "The Yankees are sending in CLASE (LHP). Pinch-hit for SMITH? YES / NO". This is Pokemon's "Will you switch?" mapped onto the real pinch-hitter chess match.

AI MANAGER, PRO (used for calibration)
- Warming: start warming when the SP is at FTG <= 40% or HP <= 45%, or ready the CL when a save spot is one inning away. At most 2 warming.
- Between innings, replace if any of these hold:
  - An SP has FTG < 10 (the main knob for the exit-cause mix).
  - An RP has FTG < 10.
  - HP <= 25%.
  - An RP has already pitched a full inning and a READY fresh arm exists.
  - The closer opens the final inning (6th or extras) with a lead of 1 to 3.
- Mid-inning, between batters only and only once the 3-batter minimum is met:
  - Pull if HP <= 20% with runners on and a READY reliever.
  - From the 5th inning, play a matchup if a READY reliever has the platoon edge on at least 2 of the next 3 batters and the current FTG <= 50%.
  - Otherwise ride him. Pro lets FTG run to the faint mid-inning, because the reliever is already READY.
- VISIT when HP <= 35% with runners on, at most once per pitcher.
- In extras, keep 1 reliever in reserve unless forced.
- Never changes pitchers mid-PA.

DIFFICULTY
- Rookie: the AI rides every pitcher to the faint, never warms anyone ahead (so its mid-inning relievers enter COLD), plays no matchups and makes no visits. Your pitchers get x1.15 HP and x1.10 FTG. Opponent numbers are visible.
- Pro: as above, with no bonuses.
- All-Star:
  - The AI warms at FTG <= 50%, pulls at FTG <= 10% or at HP <= 30% with runners on, plays matchups from the 4th, uses both visits, and pinch-hits after your pitching changes.
  - The opposing pitcher's bars show no numbers and no "tiring" hints.
- In AI-vs-AI sims, Rookie and All-Star logic must keep runs per game within +/-0.3 of Pro.
result.ui_and_text:
LAYOUT AT 390PX
Two Pokemon-style info boxes: the far one (opponent) at top left, the near one (yours) at bottom right, above the text box.
- Pitcher box: NAME, "RHP - SP", status pill, HP bar (96 x 6 px), and FTG bar (96 x 4 px) directly under it, like Pokemon's thin EXP bar.
- Your box adds numbers: "63/100" beside HP and "41/101" beside FTG.
- Batter box: name, B/T, AVG/OPS, and the count bar (3 strike pips plus 4 ball dots). No HP.
- Accessibility: each bar is role=meter with aria-valuenow and aria-valuemax and a text label ("Health 63 of 100"). Color is never the only signal.

COLORS (define as tokens with light and dark variants)
- HP: green above 50%, yellow 21 to 50%, red at 20% or below.
- FTG (a different hue family so the two bars never blur): blue above 40%, amber 16 to 40%, red at 15% or below. When empty, the bar is grey diagonal stripes plus a FUMES pill.
- Status pills, in Pokemon status style: COLD (ice blue), HURT (red), FUMES (orange), ROCKED (purple, HP 0 mid-PA).

EFFECTS
- Damage: the HP bar drains at a constant rate (a full bar takes 1.2 s, so a single hit is about 300 to 900 ms). A red "-22" rises from the bar and the sprite blinks 3 times (the Pokemon hit flicker).
- Heals: a small green "+2".
- Super effective: the existing shake. Critical: a white flash on the bar.
- FTG ticks down per pitch with no popup. At the end of a PA that cost 8 or more points, a grey "-9 FTG" pops up, which rewards grinders.
- When a bar crosses a zone it pulses once.
- When YOUR pitcher drops into HP red with sound on, play 3 short beeps once, never looping.
- Faint: the sprite drops down out of frame over 500 ms with a falling tone (original sound), and the info box slides away.
- Switch-in: an original pixel bullpen cart in team colors drives in from the outfield edge, the reliever hops out, his info box slides in, and his bars fill from 0 to full over 600 ms.
- Endure: a white flash on the bar.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no shake or drop, bars jump straight to their values, and all text stays.

TEXT LINES (exact; NAME in caps, Pokemon style)
- Pitch: "COLE used SLIDER! (87 mph)"
- After the baseball result line: "It's super effective!" / "A critical hit!" / "It's not very effective..." (wrong guess plus an out). The damage number lives in the popup, not the text.
- HP zones: "COLE is starting to feel it." (yellow) / "COLE is in trouble!" (red)
- FTG zones: "COLE is tiring." (amber) / "COLE is running low on gas!" (red) / "COLE is running on fumes!" (at 0)
- Endure: "COLE hung on! (3-batter minimum)"
- Shut-down inning: "Shut-down inning! COLE regained health!"
- Visit: "Mound visit! COLE's HP was restored by 15."
- Comebacker: "Comebacker! It hit COLE!", then "COLE is hurt, but staying in." if he survives.
- Faint, two lines: "COLE fainted!" followed by one of "He's been knocked out of the game." / "He's out of gas." / "He's hurt and leaving the game."
- Forced switch: "Choose your next pitcher." then "Go! CLASE!"
- Inheriting: "CLASE inherits a 3-1 count and 2 runners."
- Warm-up: "CLASE is still getting loose..." then "CLASE is warmed up!"
- Opponent change: "The Yankees sent out CLASE!"
- Empty bullpen: "The Yankees are out of pitchers! RIZZO takes the mound!"
- Forced removal by visit: "That's a second visit. COLE has to come out."

ENGINE EVENTS (DOM-free, on the Pick & Roll event bus, each with a snapshot)
bar, zone, endure, fumes, status, faint{cause}, change{forced, inherited}. AUTO and sim speed can skip their animations.

BOX SCORE
- Pitching columns stay IP H R ER BB K P, with an Exit code added: KO, GAS, INJ, or blank.
- Footnotes in real box-score style:
  - "Cole pitched to 2 batters in the 5th."
  - "Inherited runners-scored: Ortiz 2-1."
  - "Faints: Cole (KO, 5th, 78 P), Ortiz (GAS, 6th, 31 P)."
  - "Entered cold: Ortiz."
  - "Comebacker: Cole (3rd)."
- Play-by-play: "B5 COLE fainted (KO, HP 0/100, 78 pitches). Ortiz replaces Cole, inherits 2 runners."
- Postgame team note: "Chased their starter in the 5th."
result.editor_and_data:
DATA (data/build_data.py)
- Add per pitcher: P_start (average pitches per start) and P_relief (average pitches per relief appearance).
  - Get these from game logs: people/{id}/stats?stats=gameLog&group=pitching&season=2026.
  - Fallback: numberOfPitches divided by appearances, by role.
- Add H, BB, HBP, R and HR allowed, for LOB%.
- LOB% = (H + BB + HBP - R) / (H + BB + HBP - 1.4 x HR).
  - Blend 2026 (weight 1) with 2025 (weight 0.5).
  - Regress toward the league mean: (LOB% x BF + lgLOB% x 250) / (BF + 250).

NEW RATING: POISE (1 to 99)
- The percentile of regressed LOB% among pitchers of the same role. It is the "bends but doesn't break" or strand-rate trait.
- It drives HP_max only and never changes pitch outcomes, so calibration is safe.
- Editor shows: "Poise 72 - LOB% 77.4%".

STAMINA (EXISTING)
- Drives FTG_max.
- Editor shows: "Stamina 64 - 91 pitches/start" (or "/app" for relievers).
- The slider maps along the league's 1st to 99th percentile: SP P_start 65 to 105, RP P_relief 11 to 30.

UNCHANGED
Control, Movement and per-pitch Stuff. The bars never feed back into ratings.

EDITOR SHEET
- A derived, read-only line: "Bars: HP 104 - FTG 101".
- A preview: "Typical exit: ~84 pitches, 5.0 IP; faints from fatigue around pitch 89." This comes from the formulas, with an optional quick sim.
- Overrides keyed by player id store poise and stamina. HP_max and FTG_max are always derived at game start and never stored, so a data refresh recomputes them.
- Custom players default to Poise 50 and Stamina 50. Replacement-level fill players get Poise 35 and Stamina 40.
- Hitters get no new fields, since they have no bars.
- Export and import JSON include poise.

ENGINE CONSTANTS
One CONFIG object, not editable in the UI, holds:
- The damage and heal table.
- The multipliers and thresholds.
- The stress multipliers.
- The AI pull thresholds.
- The 3-batter carry-over flag.
- The emergency pitcher profile.

OPTIONAL "CLASSIC" HOUSE RULE (title-screen toggle)
"Faints: ON/OFF". OFF hides the bars, turns off the HP penalties, and reverts the AI manager to pitch-budget logic. It doubles as the parity test switch.

SAVE STATE (saved per pitch)
- Per pitcher in the game: hp, ftg, statuses (COLD, HURT, FUMES, ROCKED), battersFacedThisAppearance, protected flag, and warm state with its timer.
- Per team: visitsUsed, visit-per-inning log, used and fainted ids with causes.

   - Rule 9.16(h): a change at 3-1 followed by a BB charges the previous pitcher; a change at 1-1 followed by a BB charges the reliever.
   - Inherited runners are charged correctly.
   - The sum of pitcher outs equals defensive outs, runs charged equal runs allowed, and ER never exceeds R.
6. Visits: no more than 2 per game, and a second same-inning visit to the same pitcher forces removal.
7. Empty bullpen: override all 6 pitchers to HP_max 1. A position player pitches, never faints, the game completes, and the DH is terminated if the DH was used.
8. Determinism and save: the same seed gives the same bar traces. Save mid-PA with a pitcher ON FUMES and a reliever WARMING, restore, and the rest of the game is identical.

PLAYWRIGHT (390x844 and desktop)
- Full random game: no console errors, the box score adds up, and exit codes match the faint lines in the play-by-play.
- Forced switch: use ?seed= with a debug hook to set your HP to 5 and give up a hit. Expect "fainted!", then the party screen with no Cancel, the fainted pitcher marked FNT and not selectable, then "Go!" and full bars.
- Reload on the forced-switch screen: the screen reappears.
- FTG hits 0 mid-PA: the FUMES pill shows and the pitcher stays until the PA ends.
- A new reliever: BULLPEN is disabled with "1 more batter".
- The meter roles and aria values are present.
- Screenshots: bars at 60, 35 and 10%; the faint frame; the switch-in frame; the party screen; the box score footnotes.
- Reduced motion: no shake or drop classes are applied.
result.risks:
1. Tone. Pokemon lines like "COLE fainted!" can feel silly in a serious baseball sim. Every Pokemon line is paired with a plain baseball line ("He's been knocked out of the game."), and damage numbers stay in popups rather than in the narration.

2. Death spiral. Low HP, then worse control, then more walks, then more damage. The HP penalty is kept small (no more than -3 zone points, no velocity effect), the faint ends the spiral, and the "runs/PA while HP red" target watches it.

3. Faint frequency.
   - Too many faints empty bullpens and drag games out. Too few make the bars cosmetic.
   - The exit-cause and games-with-faint targets bound both sides.
   - Tune in this order: the 1.15 FTG multiplier, the Pro between-innings FTG threshold (10), then the HP_max constants.

4. Calibration drift. Real season rates already include tired innings, so stacking fatigue penalties on top would inflate runs. The fatigue centering constants and the Classic-mode parity test guard against this.

5. Rule interpretation.
   - Whether the 3-batter minimum carries over when a pitcher returns for a new inning.
   - The 9.16(h) walk-charging edge cases.
   - The position-player emergency waiving MLB's blowout/extras limit.
   Verify all three against the current rulebook, and keep them in CONFIG so they're easy to change.

6. Deferred faint. Making him finish the batter is realistic, but a player expecting an instant Pokemon faint may be confused. The FUMES/ROCKED pill plus "running on fumes!" explains it, and the human can still pull him mid-PA (inheriting the count).

7. Exploits.
   - Grinding with Take and Protect on every at-bat to drain FTG. The grinder bot target covers it.
   - Visit healing is capped at 2 per game, and a second same-inning visit forces removal.
   - Riding a pitcher to FTG 1 and then pulling him between innings is legitimate real management, not an exploit.

8. Double counting. "Super effective" already improves contact in the outcome model, and it also multiplies HP damage. This is acceptable because it affects only the bar, but watch whether pitchers feel over-punished on sat-right hits.

9. Save complexity. A pending forced switch, warm-up timers, protection flags and statuses must all persist on every per-pitch save, or reloads will break the faint flow.

10. Playback load. The per-pitch bar animations must run through the Pick & Roll playback queue so AUTO and fast sim can skip them. Headless sims emit events only.

11. IP. Use original sprites, the bullpen cart, and original faint and low-HP sounds. Don't copy Pokemon art, fonts or audio. Generic phrases are fine.

12. Box-score clutter. The extra footnotes and Exit column should collapse in a compact view on 390px screens.

result.angle: Engine and calibration first. Each pitcher carries two integer counters, HP (Health) and FAT (Fatigue, stored in tenths of a pitch). The engine changes them in exactly one place, a post-resolution step (applyBars) that runs after a pitch and its play are completely settled. It reads them in exactly one place, a pre-resolution step (barPenalties) that scales four pitcher-side inputs before the log5 combination. Bars take no draws from the main RNG. Penalties are centered on their league mean, so section 6 rates do not move. All constants live in one BARS table in engine.js, so tests can override them. The plays themselves (hit, out, run, inning, win) stay pure baseball. The bars only decide how sharp the pitcher is on the next pitch and when he has to leave. I sanity-checked the starting constants with a rough plate-appearance-level Monte Carlo (6,000 AI-vs-AI games; throwaway script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-atom/25041982-ed1b-52c3-a1a9-d5a354d2bd12/scratchpad/barsim.py). It is not the engine, so the real engine must re-run calibration, but it shows the numbers land in a sane range.
result.health_bar:
WHAT IT IS IN BASEBALL TERMS: how much punishment he has taken today, the "knocked out of the box" meter. Real managers walk out when a starter is getting shelled. Health 0 turns that moment into a rule: he has been chased. It is not a medical bar. The one literal-injury path is the comebacker below.

SIZE: HP_MAX = 100 for every pitcher (starter, reliever, closer, position player). It is an integer, and there is no new rating (see editor). Better pitchers already take less damage because they allow fewer hits, walks and runs.

DAMAGE (applied to the pitcher on the mound, only after the play is fully resolved):
- Walk 4. HBP 4. Intentional walk 0 (the manager's choice, no pitches thrown).
- 1B 6, 2B 10, 3B 12, HR 16.
- Plus 10 for EVERY run that crosses the plate while he is on the mound, however it scores (hit, walk, wild pitch, error, sac fly, steal of home). This applies whether the official scorer charges the run to him or to the pitcher before him. He gave up the hit that drove them in.
- Outs of any kind, strikeouts, fielder's choices and reached-on-error: 0 (but any runs on those plays still cost 10 each).
- Worked examples: solo HR = 26. Two-run double = 30. Grand slam = 56. Bases-loaded walk = 14. Three-run triple = 42.
- COMEBACKER (the only literal injury): on each grounder or liner in play, draw once from the AUX RNG stream. With probability COMEBACKER_P = 0.0015 the ball struck him, for 30 damage. The play's result stands exactly as already resolved; the ball is live in real baseball too. This happens about once per 30 games and causes an injury faint (INJ) about once per 250 to 400 games. It can be switched off with BARS.COMEBACKER = false.

RESTORE (only these two):
- +8 at the end of a half-inning in which no run scored while he was pitching ("settled in"), capped at 100. If he faints on the final out of the half, no heal is applied.
- +10 from a mound VISIT. This is the existing command (2 per game), and only the first visit to that pitcher in that inning heals.

Nothing else restores HP, and HP does not reset between innings. Both bars reset to full at the start of every game.

TYPICAL FLOW (sanity sim): an average starter ends his outing around 60 to 70 HP. A KO usually comes after about 5 or 6 runs in about 3 innings. That is a recognizable "knocked out" line, and it is why a run costs 10.
result.fatigue_bar:
WHAT IT IS: section 5's pitch budget made visible, weighted by stress and given a hard cap. It REPLACES section 5's separate fatigue model, so there is no double penalty. Section 4's single "HP bar = stamina" splits into Health plus this bar.

BUDGET B (in pitch-equivalents, PE), set by the Stamina rating:
- SP: B = round(60 + 0.45 x Stamina), range 60 to 105.
- RP/CL: B = round(15 + 0.30 x Stamina), range 15 to 45.
- At data build time, Stamina is set by inverting these formulas. For an SP, solve with B = real pitches per start (blended 2026/2025). For an RP, solve with B = 1.5 x real pitches per appearance. Example: 88 P/GS gives B 88 and Stamina 62. A 16-pitch reliever gives B 24 and Stamina 30.

TANK: S = round(4/3 x B). FAT_MAX = 10 x S, stored in tenths. Example: B 88 gives S 117 and FAT_MAX 1170.

DRAIN PER PITCH (tenths), applied after the pitch resolves:
- 10 base.
- +4 if any runner was on base when he threw it (pitching from the stretch, stress).
- +4 if it was his 21st or later pitch of the current inning (a laboring inning).
- The average is about 11.9 tenths, so 1.19 PE per pitch. Integer math only.
- Intentional walks cost 0 (no pitches). Pickoffs are not modeled. There is no in-game recovery: visits and clean innings do not refill gas.

ZONES:
- used = FAT_MAX - FAT.
- The budget line is used = 10 x B, which is about 25% remaining. Past it the bar is red. This is section 5's "past the budget, velocity, control and stuff fall off".
- pF = clamp((used - 10B) / (10(S - B)), 0, 1). It is 0 until the budget is spent and 1 at empty.
- An average starter left in indefinitely empties at a mean of 97 raw pitches (sim range 81 to 113, depending on traffic). A B-24 reliever empties at about 26 pitches.

POSITION PLAYER PITCHING: B 20, S 27, and he cannot faint (see faint rules).
result.performance_effects:
Penalties are read ONCE at the start of each pitch, from the bars as they stood after the previous pitch. A pitch never uses bar changes that the pitch itself causes. Only the PITCHER's inputs change. Batter rates and log5 itself are untouched.

- pF: as defined in the fatigue bar (0 until the budget is spent, 1 at empty).
- pH = clamp((40 - HP) / 40, 0, 1). It is 0 at 40 HP or more and reaches 1 at 0 HP (rattled).

CENTERING: real 2026 rates already include innings thrown tired. So every effect uses (pF - PF_MEAN) and (pH - PH_MEAN), where the means are measured over all pitches in the 2,000-game calibration run and frozen as constants. Starting values: PF_MEAN = 0.009, PH_MEAN = 0.018. As a result a fresh pitcher is a hair better than his season line, a gassed one is clearly worse, and the league average sits exactly on the data.

MULTIPLIERS (applied before log5):
1. In-zone probability (step 1): x (1 - 0.10(pF - PF_MEAN) - 0.05(pH - PH_MEAN)). Command slips and he is overthrowing.
2. Each pitch's whiff rate (step 3): x (1 - 0.20(pF - PF_MEAN)). Lost life on the stuff. Displayed velocity drops by 3 x pF mph (cosmetic only).
3. HR allowed rate (step 5): x (1 + 0.40(pF - PF_MEAN) + 0.15(pH - PH_MEAN)). Mistakes leak over the plate.
4. BABIP allowed (step 5): + 0.020(pF - PF_MEAN) + 0.010(pH - PH_MEAN), added in absolute BABIP points.
5. Wild-pitch rate: x (1 + 1.0 x pF).

SCALE: at pF = 1 a league-average arm loses 10% of zone rate and 20% of whiffs, and gives up 40% more HRs. In the middle of the red (pF 0.5) the effects are half that. Health effects are deliberately mild, which caps the snowball. With AI managers only about 4.5% of pitches have pF > 0 and about 6.7% have pH > 0. If neither side ever pulls a pitcher, scoring rises by about +0.07 runs per team per game in the sim. That is the cost of riding a tired arm.

VISIT also keeps its existing brief effect: for the next 3 pitches the pH term is treated as 0 in the zone multiplier.
result.faint_rules:
WHEN IT IS CHECKED: exactly once per pitch, after everything that pitch caused is settled. The order inside applyBars is:
(1) the pitch result, plus any batted-ball outcome, runner advancement, runs and outs (already final);
(2) the fatigue drain;
(3) health damage for the PA result and runs;
(4) the comebacker roll (AUX RNG);
(5) the FAINT CHECK;
(6) if the half-inning just ended and he is still in, the scoreless heal.

A pitcher faints when FAT <= 0 or HP <= 0. A faint never rewinds or alters the play that caused it. A walk-off ends the game before any faint is processed.

THREE-BATTER MINIMUM (OBR 5.10(g)): if he has not finished 3 PAs and the half-inning is not over:
- A Health or Fatigue zero is clamped to 1 and flagged faintDeferred. The text reads "[Name] is hanging on!"
- He faints at the first faint check after his 3rd batter's PA ends, or after the half-inning ends, whatever that PA's result was.
- An INJ faint (comebacker) is exempt and immediate, matching the rule's injury/illness exception.
- Voluntary BULLPEN is disabled under the same rule, for both the human and the AI.

MID-AT-BAT:
- Health only drops on PA-ending events, so only Fatigue (or a voluntary change) can remove a pitcher mid-PA.
- The reliever inherits the count, the runners and the outs.
- Scoring follows OBR 9.16(i). If he enters at 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2 and the batter walks, the batter and the BB go to the departed pitcher. At any other count, and for any other result (hit, out, K, HBP, error), everything goes to the reliever.

INHERITED RUNNERS (OBR 9.16(h)):
- Each runner carries responsiblePitcherId. Runs are charged to that pitcher.
- On a fielder's choice that retires an inherited runner, the batter-runner takes over that runner's responsibility.
- The extra-innings automatic runner is charged to the pitcher who started that half.
- Health damage is separate from the official charge: the pitcher on the mound takes the 10 per run, while the official ledger charges the run to whoever is responsible for that runner.

FAINT ON THE FINAL OUT: he is marked removed, and a new pitcher starts the next defensive half. No 3-batter issue arises.

REPLACEMENT:
- The human picks from a forced BULLPEN menu with no cancel (AUTO lets the AI pick). The AI uses its normal pick logic.
- The reliever enters with full bars and no cold-entry penalty. OBR 5.07(b) gives an injury replacement as many warm-ups as he needs, and every faint is treated this way.

RE-ENTRY: a removed pitcher has status removed for the rest of the game. He never appears in bullpen lists, and the engine rejects any change to him. Exception: a two-way player who was also the DH stays in the lineup as DH (OBR 5.11(b)) and only loses the mound.

EMPTY BULLPEN:
- When no unused pitcher remains, a position player must pitch.
- A bench player enters as the pitcher, and the batting order is unchanged. If the bench is empty, a fielder moves to the mound and the DH takes his position, which ends the DH.
- A human may also use a position player voluntarily under the MLB blowout rule scaled to 6 innings: trailing by 8 or more at any time, leading by 10 or more in the 6th, or in extra innings.
- A position player cannot faint: both bars floor at 1. This guarantees every game finishes.
- His ratings: Control 25, Movement 20, Stuff 10. Pitches: lob fastball at about 68 mph and an eephus at about 52 mph. Rates: K 6%, BB 12%, HR/BF 5.5%, BABIP .330.

SCORING TAGS: removedReason is KO (Health), GAS (Fatigue) or INJ (comebacker). Voluntary and AI hooks are untagged.
result.ai_and_player:
AI MANAGER (Pro). It runs at every PA boundary and at the start of each defensive half, in this order:
1. If the pitcher fainted, pick a replacement using section 5 logic (matchup, closer only in a save spot in the 6th or later, otherwise the freshest arm).
2. If the 3-batter minimum applies, make no voluntary change.
3. At the start of a half: replace the pitcher if FAT <= 25% (never send a pitcher out for a new inning in the red). Replace a reliever who already finished an inning, unless he has B >= 35 and FAT > 50% (a long man).
4. Mid-inning: replace the pitcher if FAT <= 12% or FAT <= 100 tenths (one long at-bat's worth of gas). This keeps AI fatigue faints rare.
5. VISIT: if HP <= 30, a visit is left, and this pitcher has not been visited this inning.
6. Section 5 matchup and closer moves, unchanged.

The AI NEVER pulls a pitcher on Health alone. The KO is the manager's hook for getting shelled. That keeps the parameter count low and makes faints a natural part of AI games.

AI hitters: unchanged in calibration. On All-Star only, AI hitters work the count against a tired pitcher: +5 points of take rate on 0-0 and 1-0 when the human's pitcher is at FAT <= 50%.

HUMAN ON DEFENSE:
- Sees both of his own pitcher's bars.
- Can use BULLPEN between any two pitches, even mid-PA, once the 3-batter minimum is met. A mid-PA change uses the inherited-count scoring.
- Can VISIT (heals and steadies). A second visit to the same pitcher in the same inning forces his removal (OBR 5.10(l)), and the menu warns about it.
- Can ride a gassed starter into the red and take the penalty, up to the hard cap.
- A faint opens the forced bullpen menu.

HUMAN ON OFFENSE:
- Sees the opposing pitcher's bars, so Take/Protect at-bats that run up his pitch count are a real strategy: drain his gas, chase him from the game.
- Batters never faint. The batter's bar stays the count.

DIFFICULTY (bars only, applied to the human's side only, never to plays):
- Rookie: human pitcher's Health damage x 0.75 (rounded) and fatigue drain x 0.9 (rounded), plus a "1 more hit could knock him out" warning.
- Pro: x 1.0.
- All-Star: x 1.0, plus the work-the-count hitters.

Calibration runs are always AI vs AI at Pro, so difficulty settings never touch section 6. The section 6 "sharp human-like" bot uses the AI bullpen rules above.
result.ui_and_text:
This is a minimal spec; the UI-angle design should own the details.

NAMEPLATE: the pitcher gets two stacked bars. The batter keeps the count bar plus ball/strike dots.
- Health: label "HP", number "HP 64/100". Green above 50, yellow 21 to 50, red at 20 or below. It animates down after the play.
- Fatigue: label "FATIGUE". It empties as he tires. Blue above 50%, amber 26 to 50%, red at 25% or below, with a tick mark at the budget line. Show the raw pitch count beside it ("P 74").

TEXT BOX (one line per threshold, not per hit):
- "[Name] is laboring." (Fatigue goes red)
- "[Name] is getting rattled." (HP below 40)
- "[Name] settled in." (+8)
- "Mound visit. [Name] catches his breath." (+10)
- "[Name] is hanging on!" (3-batter floor)

FAINT SEQUENCE:
- Cause line, one of: "[Name] is out of gas!" (GAS), "[Name] got knocked out!" (KO), or "Line drive off [Name]! He's shaken up." (INJ; keep it non-graphic, these are real people).
- Then "[Name] fainted!" with the Pokemon faint animation: the sprite sinks and fades, the screen dims for a moment.
- Then "The skipper signals to the pen. Now pitching: [Reliever]."
- If mid-PA: "[Reliever] inherits a 2-1 count."

BOX SCORE:
- Pitching lines get a tag: "Cole (KO) 2.2 IP 7 H 6 R 6 ER 1 BB 2 K 58 P". GAS and INJ work the same way.
- Use the real convention footnote "Cole pitched to 2 batters in the 3rd."
- Add an "Inherited runners-scored" line per reliever.

PLAY-BY-PLAY: "Cole fainted (KO). Hader replaces Cole; inherits 1-1, runners on 1st and 2nd."
result.editor_and_data:
DATA:
- Fatigue is driven only by the existing Stamina rating, which comes from the existing "average pitches per appearance" field plus GS/G.
- Role rule tightened so openers do not get starter tanks: SP only if GS >= 50% of G AND pitches per start >= 60. Everyone else is RP/CL.
- No new data fields are needed.

HEALTH: no new rating. HP_MAX = 100 for everyone. A "Durability" or "Composure" rating would not come from any real stat (breaking the brief's principle that ratings come from stats) and would add a calibration dimension. Pitcher quality already sets how much damage he takes.

EDITOR (pitcher sheet):
- The Stamina slider (1 to 99) shows read-outs beside it: "Budget 88 pitches. Red after ~74, faints ~97 (81-113)." It also shows the real source stat ("88 P/GS").
- Changing role (SP to RP) switches the B formula.
- Health shows read-only: "Health 100 (all pitchers)".
- Edits stay as overrides keyed by player id, per section 8.

ENGINE:
- One exported BARS constants object with:
  - HP_MAX 100
  - DMG {BB 4, HBP 4, IBB 0, 1B 6, 2B 10, 3B 12, HR 16, RUN 10}
  - HEAL_SCORELESS 8, HEAL_VISIT 10
  - Fatigue: base 10, runners +4, long-inning +4 after pitch 20, tank ratio 4/3
  - Budget formulas: SP 60 + 0.45 x Stamina, RP 15 + 0.30 x Stamina
  - Penalty starts: PH_START 40
  - Coefficients: zone 0.10/0.05, whiff 0.20, HR 0.40/0.15, BABIP 0.020/0.010, WP 1.0
  - Means: PF_MEAN, PH_MEAN
  - AI: hook 0.25 new inning, 0.12 mid-inning, 100 tenths absolute; visit at HP 30
  - COMEBACKER_P 0.0015, COMEBACKER_DMG 30, MIN_BATTERS 3
  - Flags: EFFECTS, FAINT, COMEBACKER (all on by default; tests toggle them)
- Per-pitcher game state: {hp, fat, fatMax, budget, bf, pitches, inningPitches, visitedThisInning, faintDeferred, status: active|removed, removedReason}.
- Per-runner state: responsiblePitcherId.
- Game state: pendingChange {side, reason, forced}.
- All of it is saved with the per-pitch save, so a reload in the middle of a forced bullpen choice reopens that menu.
- AUX RNG: a second seeded stream (game seed XOR a constant) used only for the comebacker roll.
result.calibration_and_tests:
CALIBRATION (2,000 or more AI-vs-AI games at Pro, run after the base engine passes section 6):

(a) Every section 6 target still passes with the bars on.

(b) A/B check with BARS.EFFECTS off vs on (same seeds, same AI hooks): runs per team per 6 innings differ by 0.05 or less, and K%, BB% and HR/PA each differ by 0.3 points or less. Sanity sim: 2.71 vs 2.72 runs.

(c) New targets (sanity-sim value in brackets):

| Stat | Target | Sanity sim |
|---|---|---|
| SP pitches, mean | 74 to 84 | 78.8 |
| SP pitches, SD | 9 to 15 | |
| SP pitches, 90th percentile | 98 or less | 91 |
| SP innings, mean | 4.4 to 5.1 | 4.78 |
| SP KO (Health faint) | 6 to 11% of starts | 8.3% |
| KO'd starters: mean IP | 2.5 to 3.5 | 2.9 |
| KO'd starters: mean runs allowed | 5 or more | 5.7 |
| SP GAS faint | 0.5% of starts or less | 0.03% |
| Reliever GAS faint | 1% of appearances or less | 0.5% |
| Relievers per team-game | 1.3 to 2.5 | 1.4 before matchup moves |
| AI visits per team-game | 0.2 to 0.6 | 0.39 |
| Pitches with pF > 0 | 2 to 8% | 4.5% |
| Pitches with pH > 0 | 3 to 10% | 6.7% |
| Position player pitching | 1 in 500 games or fewer | |
| INJ faints | 1 per 200 to 400 games | |

Freeze the measured PF_MEAN and PH_MEAN as constants.

(d) "Never pull" stress run (voluntary changes off for one side): a B-88 starter GAS-faints at 81 to 113 pitches (sim mean 97). The opponent scores at least 0.05 more runs per 6 innings than against AI management.

(e) KO tuning: KO rate tracks the run environment. If the engine settles at 2.9 runs and the KO rate exceeds 11%, tune DMG.RUN (9 or 10) first, then HEAL_SCORELESS.

HEADLESS UNIT TESTS (node, engine.js):
1. Exact drain, bases empty, at most 20 pitches per inning: a B-88 starter faints on exactly pitch 117. With a runner on for every pitch: exactly pitch 84 (1170 / 14 rounded up).
2. Exact damage: walk 4, solo HR 26, two-run double 30, grand slam 56, reached on error with no runs 0, scoreless half +8 capped at 100, visit +10 only once per pitcher per inning.
3. Plays are immutable. Over 20,000 random (state, seed) pairs, the resolved pitch and play (pitch result, batted ball, bases, outs, runs, count, score) is identical with bars off, on, and with DMG x 10. Diffing state before and after applyBars shows only bars, status, pendingChange and log changing.
4. Determinism: the same seed plus the same inputs give the same event-log hash and final bars across 500 seeds. Toggling COMEBACKER leaves the main-stream play-by-play identical up to the first comebacker hit.
5. Mid-PA GAS faint at 2-1: the reliever inherits 2-1; a walk is charged to the departed pitcher. At 1-2: a walk is charged to the reliever. A hit at any count goes to the reliever.
6. Inherited runners: departed pitcher leaves runners on 1st and 2nd, and the reliever allows a double. Both runs are charged to the departed pitcher; the reliever takes 30 HP. The fielder's-choice responsibility swap is checked too.
7. Three-batter rule: reliever entered at HP 30 via a test hook. HR leaves 4, the next hit clamps to 1 (deferred), and he faints after batter 3 whatever happens. He also faints immediately if the half ends first. A comebacker faints him immediately at batter 1.
8. A removed pitcher never appears in the bullpen, and attempting to use him throws an error.
9. Empty bullpen: with 7 relievers removed, the next faint brings in a position player, who never faints. 1,000 "chaos" games (DMG x 5) all finish, and every box score adds up.
10. Two-way player: if he faints as pitcher he stays in the lineup as DH.

PLAYWRIGHT (390x844):
- Force a faint through a test seed or a debug hook, then check: the forced bullpen menu has no cancel; the faint text lines and the KO/GAS tag appear in the box score.
- Reload between the faint and the reliever pick: the menu reopens with identical state.
- Bars render at both widths without overflow.
- Screenshot the faint sequence.
result.risks:
1. Double-counting fatigue. Real 2026 rates already include tired innings. Mitigated by centering on PF_MEAN/PH_MEAN plus the A/B test. If the AI hooks change later, re-measure the means.
2. Snowball ("death spiral"). Health penalties feed more damage. They are kept mild (pH starts at 40 HP, with small coefficients), and the KO itself ends the spiral. Watch the KO'd-starter runs: if the mean goes above 7, the coefficients are too strong.
3. KO frequency depends on the run environment and the AI visit policy. The sanity sim ran at 2.7 runs and the engine targets 2.9, so expect about 1 point more KOs. Retune DMG.RUN or HEAL rather than adding rules.
4. Too few faints for the fun. With AI management, GAS faints are near zero by design; only KOs happen. If players want more drama, raise PH effects or lower HP_MAX rather than making the AI careless.
5. Scoring-rule complexity: OBR 9.16(h) and 9.16(i), the fielder's-choice runner swap, the automatic runner. These are the most bug-prone part. Tests 5 and 6 cover them; the box-score "adds up" test catches drift.
6. Openers and bulk relievers in the 2026 data can get wrong tanks. Use the tightened SP role rule and the clamped B.
7. Comebacker randomness feels unfair and depicts injury to real people. Keep it rare, non-graphic, behind a flag, and on the separate AUX stream so it never perturbs the main RNG.
8. Human exploits:
   - Never pulling a starter: capped by GAS.
   - Visit spam: limited to 2 per game, one heal per pitcher per inning, and a second same-inning visit forces removal.
   - Working the count against the AI: intended baseball strategy, and the AI's hooks make it a fair fight.
9. Season mode: bars reset every game in v1. Reliever carryover between games is out of scope; adding it later needs new bullpen-availability calibration.
10. Saved games: a mid-faint save must persist pendingChange, or a reload could skip the forced change. Covered by the reload test.

per_design.design: Design 1 (Baseball realism first: HP as live Game Score, ARM as pitch budget, immediate faints)
problems: Faints are immediate, even mid at-bat. A run scoring on a WP/PB can KO a pitcher mid-count, and a GAS faint can fire on any ball or strike. Concrete illogic: a pitcher clamped at ARM 1 by the 3-batter floor is released after batter 3, throws ONE pitch to batter 4 and faints, so the reliever inherits a 1-0 count. No manager does that; he pulls him between batters. Real MLB mid-PA changes are almost all injuries (roughly 0.02-0.05% of PAs). The calibration bound 'mid at-bat changes <= 1% of PAs' is about 0.5 per 6-inning game, so it is far too loose to catch bugs.

A destroyed bar does not always faint.
