'A pitcher held at 1 stays at 1 until his next damaging event' plus per-out recovery means a pitcher whose HP was zeroed under the 3-batter floor survives indefinitely if his 3rd batter makes an out (+1/+2) or he gets a visit (+15). That contradicts the user's 'faint if the bar is destroyed'. Needed: a deferred-faint flag that forces removal at the first legal moment.

Comebacker damage is miscategorized. A non-injury comebacker drains 25-50 'composure' HP, more than a grand slam's hit damage (10). It can push HP to 0, so the box score says 'KO, shelled' for a ball that was a 1-3 putout. The RNG stream for the comebacker, its injury roll and its damage roll is also unspecified. Drawn from the main stream, those rolls perturb every later play and invalidate same-seed A/B comparisons.

The voluntary position-player rule is misstated. 'Leading by 10+' is missing the final-inning qualifier: MLB allows 10+ only in the 9th, which scales to the 6th or later. The 'emergency at any score' use is a house rule and is not labelled as one.

LAST ARM keeps an INJURED pitcher on the mound when the bench is empty. No team would do that: the DH (DH role terminated, keeps his batting spot, Rule 5.11) or a fielder (DH moves to the field) would pitch first. The design also claims termination because 'extra innings start with a runner on second', but MLB's postseason has no placed runner. If Season playoffs follow MLB, that argument fails.

Scoring gaps. (a) No 9.16(g) fielder's-choice swap: when a batter reaches on an FC or force that retires an inherited runner, the batter-runner takes over the previous pitcher's responsibility, so a per-runner chargedPitcherId alone mis-charges runs. (b) No 9.16(i): the reliever gets no benefit of prior chances for outs not accepted, so per-pitcher ER can differ from team ER. (c) The extra-inning placed runner isn't classed as 'tainted', although 9.16 deems him to have reached on an error. Who is charged for him is also unstated: it should be the pitcher who started the half, as an inherited runner if he leaves.

One counter (battersFacedThisApp) serves both the BF stat and the 5.10(g) minimum. When 9.16(h) charges a 3-1 walk to the departed pitcher, the reliever's 3-batter count must still include that batter. He pitched to him until he reached base.

Fixtures are wrong. The '1B, 1B, BB, 2B, 2-run HR = 4 runs' inning is not a legal sequence: a bases-loaded double leaves the batter on 2nd plus possibly a runner, so the HR scores 3 and the inning totals 5. It needs a stated runner out or an exact base/out script. Test 7, '2 homers in a row floor him at 1', is arithmetically impossible from 100 HP: the maximum is 42 per HR, so two leave him at 16. A forced starting HP must be specified.

'W/L/SV follow MLB exactly' is undefined for a 6-inning game. Rule 9.17(b) needs 5.0 IP for a starter's win, and this design's starter target is 4.6-5.3 IP, so roughly half of starters are ineligible. Early faints make that worse. The threshold must be stated.

Season: 'starters on normal rotation are always fresh', but nothing enforces rest days, so the human can start his ace every game. The data claim of 'no new sources' is wrong: season totals don't split pitches between starts and relief. It needs the statSplits sp/rp sitCodes or game logs.
best_ideas: HP is a Game-Score-style composure bar. Everyone starts at 100 with no new rating, and damage is a fixed table keyed only to scorebook events (result type, BB/HBP, runs, WP). Two identical singles always cost the same, and talent shows up as taking less damage.

ARM is section 5's budget made visible and replaces it, so fatigue is not double-counted. B comes from real pitches per appearance, T = B + max(8, 0.3B), there is no in-game recovery, and cost per pitch is calibrated to 1.00 so 'Budget 88' really means 88 pitches. Health affects command only; fatigue affects everything.
An explicit per-pitch order: resolve, then record (immutable), then BF++, then bars, then floors, then faint check, then inning-end recovery. The faint check runs before the dugout heal.

Correct citations and charging: 9.16(h) walk counts (2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1, 3-2; everything else and the K go to the reliever), 9.16(g) inherited runners with an IR/IRS line, and 5.10(d) no re-entry. The bars track the mound while the box score follows the rulebook: the reliever's HP drops for an inherited run that is charged to someone else.
Comebackers are allowed only on grounders and liners whose resolved result is a single or an infield out, so the narration fits. Injury is a fixed share of comebackers, independent of HP.
RUSHED only applies when nobody would plausibly have been warming. There is no penalty after an injury, which correctly reflects 5.07(b)'s unlimited warm-ups for an emergency.

Visit rules: one visit per pitcher per inning, and a second trip is routed to BULLPEN, which avoids an illegal 5.10(l) visit. 2 per game, a scaled ninth-inning bonus visit, and +1 per extra inning. Opponent bars are justified as public information (pitch count, plus hits, walks and runs).
Season carryover for relievers, plus unavailability after a GAS faint, plus a 1-5 game INJ absence.
Real box-score conventions: 'pitched to N batters in the Xth' (only when he left without recording an out in that inning), 'Inherited runners-scored', 'Pitches-strikes'. Exit tags are metadata only.
Offense drains bars only by playing baseball (no attack command). A paste-ready section 4b note directly answers the user's request.

per_design.design: Design 2 (Pokemon feel first: Poise-sized HP, FTG bar, deferred faints, warm-up states)
problems: HP damage depends on hidden and situational multipliers. 'Super effective' (the batter guessed the pitch family) multiplies hit damage by 1.5, and a 'critical' 2-out RBI multiplies run damage by 1.5. Two identical singles on the scoreboard drain different amounts of Health. That breaks 'a hit is a hit' as fans see it, and it double-counts the guess, which already improved the contact.

Run damage is '8 if earned, 4 if unearned', using the official ER classification at the moment the run scores. ER is a reconstruction under 9.16(a) and (c), and a later play in the same inning can flip a run from unearned to earned (e.g. a PB-aided run becomes earned when a later HR would have scored him anyway). The bars would need retroactive edits. Use a provisional 'tainted' heuristic instead, never the official ER.

Comebacker problems. It isn't restricted to compatible results, so 'it hit COLE' can attach to a double in the gap. INJ fires only when the 15-30 damage empties HP, so injury depends on how many runs he has allowed: a fresh pitcher can never be injured and a shelled one always is. 'Comebacker ignores Endure and causes an immediate INJ faint' is also ambiguous: does every comebacker during protection count as an injury?

A second same-inning visit is allowed with only a warning. 5.10(l) prohibits a second trip while the same batter is at bat (except after a pinch-hitter). The forced removal it causes also can't be used to get around the 3-batter minimum. Block it in both cases.

A destroyed bar can be healed back. 'A strikeout heal can lift HP to 3, which saves him' means a pitcher zeroed under Endure survives because his 3rd batter struck out, which contradicts 'faint if the bar is destroyed'.

The AI deliberately rides FTG to 0 mid-inning with a READY reliever, so the target is 25-45% of starts ending with at least one at-bat thrown ON FUMES at maximum penalties. No real manager knowingly lets a gassed starter throw his worst at-bat with a warm arm ready. 'Fainted' also becomes the label for routine pitch-limit hooks in most games, which dilutes it.

Poise comes from regressed LOB%. Strand rate is largely sequencing luck, so Health bar size (85-115) is mostly noise presented as a skill, and it adds a calibration axis the brief's 'ratings from stats' principle can't really support.

The All-Star AI 'pinch-hits after your pitching changes', and the human may change pitchers mid-PA. A pinch-hitter who enters with 2 strikes and strikes out must have the K charged to the original batter (9.15(b)). That isn't specified.

Empty-bullpen chain gaps. There's no fielder-to-mound fallback if the DH is already gone. A position player 'can't faint', so an INJ comebacker on him leaves an injured man pitching. The emergency waiver of the score limit is correctly flagged as needing verification.

Season gaps: INJ has no absence, and starters are 'always full' with no rotation rest rule. The 9.16(g) FC responsibility swap and 9.16(i) are covered only as 'charged correctly', with no spec. The paste note omits the injury/illness exemption.
best_ideas: Non-injury faints land only at PA end or half-inning end, because managers don't pull a pitcher mid-hitter. The status is ON FUMES or ROCKED until then. The AI never changes pitchers mid-PA, and the calibration target is 0 mid-PA AI changes.

Endure under 5.10(g): no faint fires while he is protected, and he faints at the boundary where protection lifts. The carry-over rule for a pitcher who returns for a new inning is a CONFIG flag, explicitly marked for checking against the current rulebook.

Reliever warm-up states: READY, WARMING, or COLD, with a penalty for getting up and down. COLD applies only when he wasn't READY, the change isn't between innings and it isn't after an injury. That is the correct use of 5.07(b).
A faint on the 3rd out means he walks off and the next pitcher enters warm. No faint is processed on a game-ending play.

Separate RNG streams for plays, flavor (comebacker) and AI. A 2,000-game test checks that every outcome event precedes its bar events and that replaying with bar events stripped gives identical plays.

The extra-inning placed runner counts as unearned for bar damage, matching 9.16 treatment. The DH moves to the mound with the DH role terminated while he keeps batting in his spot (correct under 5.11).
A Classic (faints OFF) toggle doubles as a parity test (R/G within 0.10). A grinder-bot exploit test, fatigue centering on PA-weighted modifiers, and a target of 0 mid-PA AI changes.
Every Pokemon line is paired with a plain baseball line ('He's been knocked out of the game.'). Accessibility: role=meter with aria values, and reduced-motion support.
Box score: an Exit code column, a 'Faints:' footnote, 'Comebacker:' and 'pitched to N batters' notes, and a pending forced change saved so a reload reopens the party screen.

per_design.design: Design 3 (Engine and calibration first: applyBars/barPenalties, AUX RNG, centered effects)
problems: Wrong rule citations, and Claude Code will look these up. Walk charging is 9.16(h), not 9.16(i). Inherited runners are 9.16(g), not 9.16(h). The real 9.16(i) (relief pitcher gets no benefit of previous chances for outs not accepted) is not implemented. 5.07(b) is misapplied: unlimited warm-ups apply only to a sudden emergency (injury), so 'every faint is treated this way' is false for KO and GAS. Having no cold penalty is a fine simplification, but don't cite the rule for it.

Internal contradiction: 'Health only drops on PA-ending events, so only Fatigue can remove a pitcher mid-PA' versus '10 HP for EVERY run, however it scores (wild pitch, error, steal of home)'. WP, PB and steal-of-home runs happen mid-PA, so mid-PA KOs are possible. Either defer run damage to PA end or spec mid-PA HP faints.
There is no paste-ready gameplay note. The user's literal request is 'add a gameplay mechanic note', and this design gives only the engine spec.

The comebacker rolls on every grounder or liner regardless of the resolved result, so a double down the line can be 'Line drive off [Name]!'. Flat 30 damage means INJ occurs only when HP <= 30, so injuries (and the 3-batter injury exemption) happen only to pitchers who are already being shelled.

Season: bars reset every game, with no reliever carryover and no INJ absence. A closer can pitch every day, and an 'injured' pitcher pitches tomorrow. That's illogical for a realism-claiming sim, and it makes the injury exemption free.
A second same-inning visit is allowed with a warning and forces removal. It must be blocked while the same batter is up (5.10(l)) and while the 3-batter minimum is unmet.

The budget is mislabelled. The editor says 'Budget 88 pitches', but drain averages 1.19 PE per pitch, so the red zone starts after about 74 real pitches. Penalties begin about 14 pitches before his real average outing, and the label tells the player something false.

Test 3 says the play is identical 'with bars off, on, and DMG x10'. EFFECTS changes pre-pitch probabilities, so a red-bar state resolves differently with effects off. The test must be scoped to applyBars only (same pre-pitch state, any DMG), or it will fail or test nothing.

Undefined edge cases: an INJ comebacker on a position-player pitcher (who 'cannot faint'); no 9.15(b) rule for 2-strike pinch-hitters if pinch-hitting mid-PA is possible; and the 6-inning win threshold (9.17(b) needs 5 IP against a 4.4-5.1 IP target).
best_ideas: One write point (applyBars, post-resolution) and one read point (barPenalties, pre-resolution, pitcher inputs only, before log5). That makes 'bars never alter a play' provable. The comebacker uses an AUX RNG, and a state-diff test checks that only bars, status, pendingChange and the log change.

faintDeferred: a bar zeroed under the 3-batter minimum is clamped to 1 and flagged, and he faints at the first check after his 3rd completed PA or the half-inning end, whatever that PA's result. This is faithful to 'destroyed bar = faint' and to 5.10(g).
9.16(g) fielder's-choice responsibility swap. The extra-inning placed runner is charged to the pitcher who started the half. Health damage is kept separate from the official ledger.

Position-player use is scaled correctly: trailing by 8+ at any time, leading by 10+ in the 6th, or extra innings. Fielder to mound with the DH moving to the field (DH terminated) when the bench is empty. A two-way SP/DH stays as DH (5.11(b)).
Flat damage by result type plus a flat 10 per run means no real-time ER classification is needed and there is nothing to revise retroactively.

Centering: effects use (pF - PF_MEAN) and (pH - PH_MEAN), checked by an A/B run with EFFECTS off vs on (R within 0.05; K%, BB% and HR/PA within 0.3). KO targets read like a real knockout line (mean 2.5-3.5 IP, 5+ runs).
Exact drain fixtures: a B-88 starter faints on pitch 117 with bases empty and pitch 84 with a runner on every pitch. The SP role rule is tightened so openers don't get starter tanks.
pendingChange is persisted so a reload reopens the forced bullpen menu. A walk-off ends the game before any faint is processed.

must_haves: The paste-ready gameplay note goes in section 4, replacing 'pitcher's bar is stamina', and section 5's Fatigue line points to it. It says: it is still baseball, a hit is a hit, and runs, outs, innings and the win are pure baseball. Pitchers only have two bars, Health and Fatigue. A destroyed bar = faint = forced out of the game (knocked out, out of gas, or injured). Substitutions follow MLB rules. Batters never faint, and their bar is the count.

Order per pitch: resolve and record the play (immutable), then update the bars, then apply the 3-batter floor, then the faint check, then inning-end recovery. Bars are read only before the next pitch (one read point, one write point), and they affect only pitcher inputs on future pitches. All bar randomness (comebacker, injury roll, damage roll) uses a separate seeded AUX RNG stream.

HP damage is a fixed function of what the official scorer records: result type, BB/HBP (IBB 0), WP, and runs scoring while he is on the mound (inherited runs included). No multipliers for the batter's guess or for game situation. Any earned/unearned discount uses a provisional 'tainted' heuristic (runner reached on error, scored on E/PB, or the extra-inning placed runner), never the official ER, which can change retroactively within an inning.

A destroyed bar always faints. If the 3-batter minimum blocks removal, clamp the bar to 1 and set faintDeferred. He leaves at the first legal moment (after his 3rd completed PA or when the half ends), whatever that PA's result. No out, K, inning-end or visit recovery can cancel a deferred faint.

Non-injury faints take effect at the PA boundary: he finishes the batter ON FUMES or ROCKED, at maximum penalties. The AI never changes pitchers mid-PA except for injury. Mid-PA changes happen only on the human's voluntary BULLPEN (after the minimum is met) or after an injury, with a calibration target of at most 0.05% of PAs for AI vs AI.

Rule 5.10(g): the 3-batter minimum applies to starters and relievers. It counts completed PAs (retired or reached base, IBB included), including a batter inherited mid-count. It is tracked separately from the BF stat that 9.16(h) assigns. It is satisfied by the end of the half-inning, and a pitcher who returns for a new inning continues his cumulative count (CONFIG flag, verified against the rulebook). It is exempted only by INJ.

Rule 9.16(h): if the count at the change was 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2 and the batter walks, the BB and that batter-runner go to the departed pitcher. Every other result, and every result from any other count (including the K), goes to the reliever.

Rule 9.16(g): inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on. That includes the fielder's-choice/force swap: a batter who reaches on an FC that retires an inherited runner takes over that responsibility. An inherited runner caught stealing or picked off transfers nothing. The reliever's line shows IR/IRS.

Rule 9.16(i): the reliever gets no benefit of previous chances for outs not accepted, so per-pitcher ER can differ from team ER. Box-score tests must check ER <= R per pitcher and sum of pitcher R = team R, but must NOT assert that the sum of pitcher ER equals team ER.

The extra-inning placed runner counts as reached on error for 9.16 (unearned). He is charged to the pitcher who started that half (inherited if that pitcher leaves). He is not a batter faced and does not count toward the 3-batter minimum. If Season playoffs follow MLB (no placed runner), termination must not depend on him: keep the sim safety cap.

No re-entry (5.10(d)). A removed pitcher can't move to a field position. The engine rejects re-entry, and the UI shows him greyed out as FNT/USED. If two-way SP/DH players are supported, a removed two-way pitcher stays in as DH (5.11(b)).

Visits: 2 per game, plus 1 in the 6th if both are already used, plus 1 per extra inning. One visit per pitcher per inning. A second trip is blocked while the same batter is up (5.10(l)) and while the 3-batter minimum is unmet; otherwise it routes to BULLPEN.

Comebackers can only attach to grounders and liners whose already-resolved result is a single or an infield out. Injury is a fixed share of comebackers, independent of current HP. A non-injury comebacker does little or no HP damage and can never produce a KO label. INJ bypasses the 3-batter minimum, and his replacement gets unlimited warm-ups (5.07(b)): no cold or rushed penalty after an injury. Any cold-entry penalty applies only to non-injury forced entries.

Empty bullpen, in order: unused pitchers (excluding rested starters in Season), then an unused bench player, then the DH to the mound (DH terminated, keeps his batting spot), then a fielder to the mound with the DH moving to the field, then LAST ARM. Never leave an INJ pitcher on the mound while any of those options exist, and skip injury rolls for position-player pitchers. Voluntary position-player use is allowed only when trailing by 8+, leading by 10+ in the 6th or later, or in extra innings. Emergency use at any score is labelled a house rule.

Fatigue REPLACES section 5's fatigue (one system, no double-count). The budget is in real pitches, with the average cost per pitch calibrated to 1.00 so editor labels like 'Budget 88 pitches' are literally true. No in-game recovery.
A faint on the 3rd out means no mid-inning entry, and the reliever starts the next defensive half. A faint on the game's final out or a walk-off processes no replacement and is only logged.

Batters: no Health or Fatigue bar, no fainting, and the batter bar stays the count. The offense drains pitcher bars only by playing baseball. If mid-PA pinch-hitting is possible, 9.15(b) applies: a 2-strike substitute who strikes out has the K charged to the original batter.

Season mode: INJ costs an IL-style absence of several games, relievers carry over workload and become unavailable after back-to-back days, and starters need rotation rest days. Otherwise 'always fresh' becomes an exploit.
State the starter-win threshold for 6-inning games explicitly: 9.17(b) needs 5.0 IP, or a declared scaled value. A fainted pitcher keeps his line and can still be the pitcher of record.

Box score: exit tags (KO/GAS/INJ) are metadata only, plus 'X pitched to N batters in the Yth' (only when he left without recording an out in that inning), 'Inherited runners-scored', and 'Pitches-strikes'. Pitches thrown before a mid-PA change count for the departed pitcher.

Correct rule citations in the brief: 5.07(b) warm-ups, 5.10(d) re-entry, 5.10(g) 3-batter minimum, 5.10(l) second visit, 5.11 DH termination, 9.15(b) 2-strike pinch-hitter, 9.16(g) inherited runners and FC, 9.16(h) walk charging, 9.16(i) relief ER, 9.17(b) starter win.

New calibration targets must be consistent with section 6's 3.9 P/PA (about 16.5 pitches per inning): starter IP and pitches, pitchers per team-game, KO, GAS and INJ rates, AI mid-PA changes about 0, visits per game, and an A/B check with effects off vs on (R/G within 0.05-0.10; K%, BB% and HR/PA within 0.3-0.5 points). Unit fixtures must be legal base/out scripts with explicit starting bars.
must_avoid: Any bar, status or faint changing a resolved or recorded play, an official scoring decision, or an outcome probability of the pitch that caused the bar change.
HP damage multipliers based on the batter's hidden guess ('super effective') or game situation ('critical' 2-out RBI). Identical scorebook events must cost identical HP.
Using official earned/unearned status as a live bar input (it can flip retroactively within an inning).
Letting a pitcher whose bar was destroyed stay in once the 3-batter minimum is met, or heal back from a clamped 1 via outs, a K, inning-end recovery or a visit.
Routine mid-PA AI pitching changes, faints firing on a ball, strike or foul (except injury), and loose bounds like '<= 1% of PAs'.
Comebackers on extra-base hits or fly balls. Injury probability that depends on current HP. Comebacker damage larger than a home run's that can be labelled a KO.
Keeping an injured pitcher on the mound while a bench player, the DH or a fielder could pitch.
A second same-inning visit while the same batter is at bat, or one used to remove a pitcher before the 3-batter minimum.
Treating KO or GAS faints as injuries for the 3-batter exemption, or citing 5.07(b) unlimited warm-ups for non-injury changes.
Misnumbered rule citations (walk charging is 9.16(h), not (i); inherited runners are 9.16(g), not (h)).
Stacking the new fatigue bar on top of section 5's old fatigue model (double-counting tiredness that real rates already contain).
Drawing bar randomness from the main play RNG.
Any bar, fainting or bar-driven outcome modifier on batters.
Voluntary position-player pitching when leading by 10+ before the final inning.
Box-score tests that assume the sum of pitchers' ER equals team ER.
Relying on the extra-inning placed runner to guarantee games end if playoffs follow MLB postseason rules.
New pitcher ratings that rest on noise-dominated stats (e.g. Poise from LOB%) driving bar size.
Season modes where injured pitchers are available the next game or starters can start every day.
Editor labels in 'pitch-equivalents' presented as real pitch counts.

per_design.design: Design 1 (Baseball realism first: HP = Game-Score-style command/composure, ARM = visible pitch budget)
problems: The AI Health hook makes KO faints almost impossible. Pro pulls at HP<=20, or HP<=35 with a runner on, at every PA boundary. The largest one-PA hit is 42 (grand slam: 10 + 4x8), so a pitcher above the hook line cannot reach 0 in one PA. My PA-level sim (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-atom/25041982-ed1b-52c3-a1a9-d5a354d2bd12/scratchpad/critic_sim.py, 4,000 games, effects off): starter KO 0.0%, Health hooks 8.1%, any faint in only 4.9% of games. Its own target 'KO 0.5-3% of appearances' cannot be met, and in AI play the user's 'pitchers can faint' mechanic is mostly invisible.

Several of its own targets fail in the sim. AI visits are 0.16 per team-game against a 0.3-1.0 target. Relief out-of-gas faints are about 2.0% of relief appearances against 0-0.5%. Pitchers per team-game are 2.29 against 2.3-3.2.

The reliever tank is too small: T = B + 8 gives 25 for a 17-pitch reliever and 20 for a B=12 specialist. The 3-batter minimum plus one long inning routinely reaches that, so relievers get pinned at the 'hanging on' floor and go out of gas mid-PA. Real one-inning relievers sometimes reach 30-35 pitches.

Faints can land mid-PA. ARM runs out on a ball or foul, and HP drops on runs that score on a wild pitch, passed ball, steal or balk. That puts the inherited-count path into AI-vs-AI games. The target 'mid-PA changes <= 1% of PAs' is about 0.4 per game, orders of magnitude above MLB, where mid-PA changes are nearly always injuries.

Fatigue math uses floats (0.90 / 0.20 / 0.40). Its own fixture 'runner on, 10 pitches: U = 11.0' fails exact equality in IEEE (0.9 + 0.2 = 1.1000000000000001). Threshold checks such as U>=B and O=0 become off-by-one-pitch flaky.

The worked fixtures are not exact, so they cannot be unit tests. '1B, 1B, BB, 2B, 2-run HR' is impossible as written: a bases-loaded double that scores 2 leaves runners on 2nd and 3rd, so the homer scores 3. 'A 2-run inning costs a net 30' depends on which events happened. Every fixture needs an explicit event script with base and out states.

The comebacker has no per-ball-in-play probability, so 'struck in 2% of team-games' cannot be tested. The RNG stream for the strike roll and the 25-50 damage roll is not specified; drawing from the main stream changes every later play when the flag is toggled.
The saved state has no pending forced change. A reload while the forced bullpen picker is open, before a reliever is chosen, is unspecified. RNG stream states are not listed either.

3-batter floor inconsistency: a pitcher held at 1 HP who then gets a strikeout (+2) is at 3 HP and stays in. A pitcher who was effectively knocked out survives because of rule timing, which no fan would read as baseball.

RUSHED is almost dead code. A KO from HP>50 in one PA is impossible (maximum 42), and a GAS faint from U<B in one PA is impossible for starters (T-B >= 26). It still gets a dedicated test and UI chip.

Health regenerates very fast: +1 per out, +2 per strikeout, +4 per half and +6 more if scoreless. Health sits near 100 most of the game (in the sim, only 2% of starters ever drop to 20 or below), so the Pokemon chip-damage feel is weak. The design admits this.
Effects are not centered. 'Tune base rates with effects on' moves individual pitchers off their real lines to absorb the bar penalties, and there is no A/B check of effects on vs off.

The role split of pitches per appearance is described as needing 'no new sources'. Season totals mix starts and relief outings for swingmen, so it actually needs statSplits (sitCodes sp/rp) or game logs.
A position player who pitches can himself be knocked out and replaced by another position player. The voluntary rule omits 'in the final inning' from 'leading by 10+'.
Season carryover and 1-5 game injuries add scope and a new calibration surface that the user did not ask for.
best_ideas: Clean split of effects. Health affects command only (walks, mistakes, wild pitches). Fatigue affects velocity, stuff, command and contact quality. Low Health stays separate from fatigue and does not double-count the times-through-the-order decline.

ARM is section 5's budget made visible, with the mean cost per pitch normalized to 1.00 +/- 0.03, so B still means real pitches. The budget tick sits on the bar, and T = B + max(8, 0.3B) is the hard ceiling for starters (about 110-120 pitches).
An exact post-pitch order: resolve, record as immutable, count batters faced, apply bars, apply floors, faint check, then the inning-end heal. The faint check comes before the dugout heal.
Comebackers only on results that match the narration (singles up the middle, infield outs), with the injury as a separate roll that does not depend on current HP.
Bar colors match the active penalty tiers. Bars drain only after the result line has been narrated. Opponent bars are shown because the information is public in real baseball.

Real box-score conventions: exit tags (KO/GAS/INJ), 'pitched to N batters in the Xth', IR-IRS and pitches-strikes lines. Per-runner chargedPitcherId. 9.16(h) walk charging, with the batter-runner charged to the departed pitcher.
Controlled effect checks use forced states and the same pitcher-batter pairs to avoid selection bias. Includes a 'Ride him' bot and a 25-inning sim safety cap.
Mound visits follow MLB: 2 per game, a bonus visit in the final inning and one more per extra inning. A second same-inning visit to the same pitcher forces his removal (5.10(l)).
Error-tainted runs cost half Health, which is fair to the pitcher in baseball terms. Intentional walks cost 0.

per_design.design: Design 2 (Pokemon feel first: HP + FTG, frequent faints, warm-up system)
problems: Faints are frequent by design and the AI rides starters on purpose. Pro 'lets FTG run to the faint mid-inning', with targets of GAS faints in 25-45% of starts and a faint in 50-75% of games. Every GAS faint includes a PA thrown ON FUMES at full penalties, so the AI is regularly using a pitcher it knows is spent, which a real manager would not do. The sim reproduces it: GAS 29.5% of starts, a faint in 66% of games.

Health drains steadily with workload. The net is about -2.2 per PA, and the only between-innings recovery is +5 for a 1-2-3 inning, so HP works as a second fatigue meter. In the sim, 57% of starters fall to 50% HP or lower, where the Health penalty applies, and 21% fall to 20% or lower. That double-counts tiredness with FTG, and the Health penalties are not centered (only the fatigue modifiers are).

Too many starters leave on Health. In the sim, 15.2% of starts end in a Health hook and another 4.4% in a KO, about 20% in total, which is well above the real rate of starters chased for getting shelled. Starts under 3 IP are 9.9%, failing its own 4-8% target. Pitchers per team-game are 2.48, failing its 2.7-3.5. Empty bullpens are about 1% of team-games with 5 relievers, failing its <=0.3%.

The fatigue ramp starts at 40% FTG remaining, around pitch 54 for an average starter. That changes section 5's 'falls off past the budget', which the user did not ask for. Centering then makes fresh pitchers better than their real lines, which creates a pull-early exploit for a human who uses the bullpen aggressively. The Classic ON/OFF parity test does not say which fatigue model applies when faints are OFF.

'Super effective' (x1.5) and 'critical hit' (two-out RBI, x1.5) Health multipliers depend on the batter's hidden guess and on a situational rule. The right guess has already improved the outcome, so this double-counts it, and a fan cannot see why the same single hurts more.

The Poise rating comes from regressed LOB%, which is mostly luck. It needs per-pitcher game-log pulls (hundreds of API calls). It changes when pitchers are hooked or knocked out, and therefore who pitches, so the claim that it is calibration-safe is false.

The warm-up subsystem (WARMING/READY/COLD, a 15% penalty for 'up and down', 2 warming at once, timers) is scope creep. It adds calibration surface (the COLD penalty), save-state timers and AI logic. A reliever who never sits down can stay READY forever at no cost, which is an exploit.
A modal 'Pinch-hit for X?' prompt after every opponent pitching change interrupts play constantly.
Endure inconsistency: a strikeout heal can lift a floored pitcher to 3 HP and 'save' him, so the knocked-out state is undone by rule timing.
An injury happens only if comebacker damage empties HP, so the chance of injury depends on how badly he has pitched, which has no baseball logic. A survivor also gets HURT (x1.25 drain).

HP_max varies by role and by Rookie difficulty (x1.15 HP, x1.10 FTG), and FTG_max is stress-weighted at an average of 1.13. B no longer reads as pitches, and the numbers on the bar ('41/101') are not pitches.
The saved state keeps no count at the time of the change for 9.16(h), so the departed pitcher's walk charge cannot be reconstructed after a reload.
best_ideas: Non-injury faints land only at a PA end or half-inning end. A bar that hits 0 mid-PA becomes ON FUMES or ROCKED, and he finishes the batter ('managers don't pull a guy mid-hitter unless he's hurt'). Target: 0 mid-PA AI-vs-AI changes. The inherited-count path then comes only from a human's voluntary mid-PA change.
pendingForcedChange is saved per pitch, so a reload reopens the forced party screen. The forced screen has no Cancel, FNT/USED pitchers are greyed out and cannot be selected, then 'Go! X!'.
Separate RNG streams for play, flavor (comebacker) and AI, plus a test that every outcome event comes before its bar events across 2,000 seeded games.
Bot targets: a 'grinder' bot whose win rate must not exceed the sharp bot's, a death-spiral guard (runs per PA while HP is red <= 1.15x league), and 'ON FUMES PAs <= 3%, wOBA <= league + .060'.
The ambiguous rulings (3-batter carryover across innings, 9.16(h) edge cases, position-player emergency limits) are flagged as needing verification and kept as CONFIG flags.
A position player who pitches cannot faint (bars floor at 1). The DH-to-mound case ends the DH under the real rule.

Accessibility: role=meter with aria-valuenow, a text label, color never the only signal, and a reduced-motion path. Engine events (bar, zone, endure, faint{cause}, change{forced, inherited}) go through the Pick & Roll playback queue so AUTO and fast sim can skip them.
Health run damage goes to the pitcher on the mound while the official charge follows 9.16(g). The extra-inning placed runner is treated as unearned.
A stress-weighted drain (traffic, long PAs, long innings) is good baseball logic for 'high-stress innings'.

per_design.design: Design 3 (Engine and calibration first: integer bars, single apply/read points, centered penalties)
problems: Internal contradiction: 'Health only drops on PA-ending events' conflicts with '10 for EVERY run ... wild pitch, error, steal of home', because those runs score mid-PA. HP can therefore reach 0 mid-PA, and the faint timing for that case is unspecified.

Mid-PA GAS faints are still possible in AI games. The mid-inning hook checks at PA boundaries with up to 100 tenths left, and a long PA with traffic costs 14 tenths per pitch, so the inherited-count path reaches AI play. Faints should be deferred to the PA end instead.

Drain averages 11.9 tenths, i.e. 1.19 units per pitch, while B is set to real pitches per start. The 'budget' then turns red around 74 real pitches for a pitcher who really averages 88. The editor line 'Budget 88 pitches. Red after ~74' contradicts itself, and every starter is shortened relative to his real budget.

KO frequency is fragile. Under the stated constants its own sim reproduces (KO 7.6-7.9%, 79 pitches, 4.8 IP), but only with undocumented environment variables. The script defaults (RUN_DMG=6, HOOK=0.22, NEWINN=0.30, VISITS=0) give KO 1.9-5.5% and a reliever GAS rate of 2.4%. That run was at 2.7 R/G with 7 relievers, not the brief's 2.9 and about 5, and with coefficients that differ from the spec (no centering, bbm 0.30pF, HR pH 0.10). In my variant at 2.98 R/G, 5 relievers and drain normalized to 1.0, KO rose to 11-13%, above its 6-11% band, and relievers per team-game fell to 0.88, below its 1.3-2.5 band.

Rule citations are swapped. Inherited runners are OBR 9.16(g), not 9.16(h). Walk charging after a mid-count change is 9.16(h), not 9.16(i). 9.16(i) is the rule that a reliever gets no benefit from earlier errors, so a pitcher's ER can differ from the team's ER, and no design accounts for that in its 'box score adds up' tests.

An injury happens only if the 30-point comebacker empties HP, so it effectively requires HP <= 30. Getting hurt then depends on pitching badly, and a healthy pitcher who is struck takes 30 Health and becomes likelier to be 'chased'. Neither has baseball logic. The roll also fires on any grounder or liner regardless of the resolved result, so the narration can conflict (for example a comebacker on a double down the line).

The low end of the reliever budget is too small. B = 15 + 0.3 x Stamina with a minimum of 15 gives a tank of 20 units, about 17 pitches, which clashes with the 3-batter minimum (frequent deferred GAS faints and fumes pitching).

Test 3, 'identical with bars off, on', is ambiguous: when pre-pitch modifiers are nonzero, effects legitimately change probabilities. It must say the modifiers are held equal (or EFFECTS is fixed) and only the post-resolution bar logic varies.

The per-pitcher saved state has no count at the time of the change or departed pitcher id for 9.16(h). A reload mid-PA after a voluntary change loses the walk charge. The AUX RNG is derived from the seed, but its position must also be saved per pitch.
The Health text threshold (below 40) does not match the Health colors (yellow at 21-50, red at 20 or below), so color no longer means 'penalty active'.

Health accumulates (only a scoreless half heals +8). In my variant 55% of starters dropped to 50 or below and about 25% to 20 or below. The penalty starts at 40, so a meaningful share of late-inning starter pitches is penalized by Health, which correlates with workload. It is mild, but the A/B test must actually guard it.
Test 9 removes 7 relievers, but the brief says about 5. Season mode has no reliever carryover, so the closer can pitch every game (acceptable for v1 if stated).
best_ideas: Architecture: bars are written in exactly one place (applyBars, after the play is fully settled) and read in exactly one place (barPenalties, before log5, pitcher inputs only). One exported BARS table that tests can override, plus EFFECTS, FAINT and COMEBACKER flags.

Integer tenths for fatigue and integer HP give exact fixtures (a B-88 starter faints on pitch 117 with the bases empty, pitch 84 with a runner on every pitch) and threshold checks that are never flaky.

Penalties centered on the measured mean (PF_MEAN, PH_MEAN), plus an A/B check with EFFECTS off vs on (same seeds, same hooks): R/G within 0.05, and K%, BB% and HR/PA within 0.3 points. This keeps both the league and each pitcher on his real line.

The AI never pulls on Health at Pro: 'the KO is the manager's hook'. HP 0 then means 'chased', faints are visible and meaningful (about 1 game in 5), and run-based damage (about 5-6 runs gets him knocked out) matches the real 'knocked out of the box' line.

faintDeferred under the 3-batter rule: the bar clamps at 1, and he faints after his 3rd batter's PA or at the end of the half, whatever the result. That is exactly how a real manager is forced to wait. Injury is exempt and immediate.

Health damage is a plain, legible table with no new rating (HP_MAX 100 for all). It drops after every hit, so the bar visibly moves; a scoreless half heals +8 ('settled in') and a visit +10, once per pitcher per inning.
The fielder's-choice responsibility swap (9.16(g)) and the extra-inning placed runner charged to the pitcher who started the half are both covered.
An AUX RNG stream only for the comebacker, with a test that the main-stream play-by-play is identical until the first comebacker.
Plays-immutable test by diffing state before and after applyBars (only bars, status, pendingChange and log may change). 1,000 'chaos' games (DMG x5) must all finish with box scores that add up.
Difficulty changes only the human side's bars (Rookie: damage x0.75, drain x0.9) and All-Star hitters. Calibration is always Pro AI vs AI, so section 6 is untouched by difficulty.

Pitchers removed by the AI's hooks carry no exit tag. Two-way players lose only the mound (5.11(b)). Position players cannot faint, and the voluntary position-player rule is scaled to 6 innings (trailing 8+, leading 10+ in the 6th, extras). A sanity sim ships with numbers.

must_haves: The baseball result always comes first. resolvePitch reads bars only through one pre-pitch modifier function, and applyBars runs once after the pitch and its play are final. Bars never edit, re-roll or upgrade a recorded result. Test: diff the state before and after applyBars; only bar, status, pendingChange and log fields may change.

Two pitcher bars only. HEALTH is how hard he has been hit today, the baseball 'knocked out of the game / chased' meter, not physical health. FATIGUE is section 5's pitch budget made visible and is the only fatigue system: delete section 5's separate falloff path and replace the section 4 line 'pitcher's bar is stamina'. Batters never faint; their bar stays the count.

Fatigue uses integer tenths. Normalize the drain so the league-average cost is 10 tenths (1.00 +/- 0.02 units) per pitch, which keeps B in real pitches. Use a base of about 8.5, +2.5 with runners on and +3.5 from the 21st pitch of an inning, tuned to the mean. Penalties start only past B, unchanged from section 5. Tank ceiling for starters is about 1.3B. Relievers get a tank floor of about 30 raw pitches so the 3-batter minimum plus one long inning fits.

Health is integer, HP_MAX 100 for everyone, and has no new rating. Damage comes from the result type (walk/HBP 4, single 6, double 10, triple 12, homer 16) plus a fixed amount per run scored while he is on the mound, inherited runners included; error-tainted runs can cost half. Recovery: a scoreless half and a mound visit. Health penalties affect command and mistakes only and stay mild.

Non-injury faints happen only at the end of a PA or a half-inning. A bar that empties mid-PA shows 'running on fumes' or 'rocked' and he finishes the batter. Mid-PA run damage applies immediately, but its faint waits for the PA to end. AI-vs-AI mid-PA pitching changes must be exactly 0 by construction. The inherited-count path (9.16(h)) is still implemented for a human's voluntary mid-PA change.

Each bar has one hook concept. At Pro, Health 0 IS the manager's hook (no separate AI Health pull above 0), so KO faints are visible and mean 'chased'. The AI's fatigue hook sits near B, and a GAS faint is the ceiling for riding a pitcher too long (rare under AI). Difficulty may make the AI's hooks quicker or slower but never changes the rules.

3-batter minimum (5.10(g)) is enforced with a deferred faint. A bar reaching 0 before batter 3 clamps at 1 with faintDeferred=true. He faints after his 3rd batter's PA or at the end of the half, whatever that PA's result, and no heal can cancel it. Injury is exempt and immediate. Voluntary BULLPEN is disabled, with the reason shown. Whether the minimum carries over into the next inning is a CONFIG flag, with its default verified against the current rulebook.

Correct rule citations and behavior. 5.10(d): no re-entry; the engine rejects it and the UI greys the pitcher out as FNT/USED. 5.10(l): a second same-inning visit to the same pitcher removes him. 9.16(g): inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on, including the fielder's-choice swap. 9.16(h): at 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2, a walk and that batter-runner go to the departed pitcher; everything else goes to the reliever. 9.16(i): a reliever gets no benefit from earlier errors (per-pitcher ER may differ from team ER). The extra-inning placed runner is unearned and charged to the pitcher who started the half.
Health run damage goes to the pitcher on the mound even when the official run is charged to someone else. Bars track what happened on the mound; the box score follows the rulebook.

Separate seeded RNG streams for play, AI and aux/flavor (the comebacker). The comebacker, if kept, is an independent rare roll (about 1 injury per 250-500 games), only on results that match the narration, never dependent on current HP, non-graphic, and behind a flag. Save every stream's state with each per-pitch save.

Per-pitch save includes, per pitcher: hp, fatigue used (int), budget, tank, batters faced this appearance, inning pitch count, faintDeferred, fumes/rocked, visitedThisInning, status, and exit reason/inning. Per team: visits left. Per runner: responsible pitcher id. For a live PA: count at change and departed pitcher id. pendingForcedChange with its cause. A reload while the forced picker is open reopens it and re-shows the faint lines.

Forced replacement Pokemon-style: the forced picker has no Cancel ('Choose your next pitcher' / 'Go, X!' / 'Now pitching for Seattle: X'), with the coach's pick highlighted, and AUTO picks for the human.

Empty bullpen chain: an unused pitcher, then a bench position player, then a fielder moves to the mound (the DH role ends under the real rule). A position player who pitches cannot faint (bars floor at 1), so every game completes. Add a sim-only safety cap. The voluntary position-player rule is scaled to 6 innings: trailing by 8+, leading by 10+ in the 6th, or extra innings.

Bars animate only after the result line is narrated. Bar colors equal the active penalty tiers. Fatigue shows the real pitch count and a budget tick. Exit tags KO/GAS/INJ appear in the box score with real footnotes ('pitched to N batters in the Xth', inherited runners-scored). Bars use role=meter and aria values, and there is a reduced-motion path.

Calibration is run AI vs AI at Pro with bars and effects ON, and every section 6 row still passes. A/B with effects off vs on (same seeds, same hooks): runs per team per 6 innings within +/-0.05, and K%, BB% and HR/PA within +/-0.3 points. Measured penalty means are frozen as centering constants, or the A/B result proves they aren't needed.

New calibration targets: starter pitches mean 76-88, SD 10-16, p90 <= 102. Starter IP mean 4.6-5.3 of 6. Starts under 3.0 IP (non-injury) 4-8%. Health KO faints 6-10% of starts and <= 3% of relief appearances. KO'd starters average 2.3-3.7 IP and 5.0-7.0 runs (death-spiral guard). GAS faints <= 1% of starts and <= 1% of relief appearances. Games with at least one faint (either team) 12-25%. Injury faints 1 per 250-500 games (0 with the flag off). Mid-PA non-injury changes AI vs AI exactly 0. Pitchers per team-game 2.0-3.0. Relief share of innings 12-25%. Pitches thrown past budget 1-6%. Pitches with a Health penalty active 3-10%. Runs per PA while the Health penalty is active <= 1.15x league. AI visits 0.2-0.8 per team-game. Position player pitching <= 1 per 300 team-games, and 100% of games complete.

Tune KO frequency only after the run environment passes. Tune the per-run damage first, then the scoreless heal. KO rate rises steeply with runs per game (about 8% at 2.7 R/G vs about 12% at 3.0 R/G in my sim).

Strategy bots: 'never pull' (the starter GAS-faints within T to T+8 units, and the opponent scores +0.10 to +0.50 runs per 6 innings more than against AI management). 'Pull early' (pulls at 0.8B; win rate within +/-2 points of the standard bot, so there is no centering exploit). 'Grinder' (always Take/Protect; win rate <= the sharp bot's). The sharp human-like bot still wins 60-65% at Pro using the Pro bullpen policy.

Exact unit fixtures written as event scripts with explicit base and out states and integer expected values, covering: the damage table, drain to the exact faint pitch, 3-batter deferral, 9.16(h) at 3-1 vs 1-2, inherited runners plus the fielder's-choice swap, no re-entry, empty-bullpen completion, visit limits, inning-ending faint (no mid-inning entry), and save/restore at every pitch giving an identical continuation. Tests must not assert that the sum of pitcher ER equals team ER.

One constants object in engine.js holds every bar number (damage, heals, drain terms, tank ratio, reliever tank floor, tiers, effect coefficients, centering means, AI hook thresholds per difficulty, visit counts, comebacker rate) plus the EFFECTS, FAINT and COMEBACKER flags. A test-only debug hook forces bar states for Playwright.

Data: Stamina drives the budget from real pitches per start or per relief appearance, split by role via statSplits (sitCodes sp/rp) or game logs, with a fallback, blended 2026 x1 and 2025 x0.5. Editor read-out, e.g. 'Stamina 62 · 88 P/GS → budget 88, ceiling ~115'. Health shows read-only as 100.

The paste-ready note says it plainly: it's still baseball; a hit is a hit; runs, outs, innings and the win are pure baseball. Fainting is the Pokemon name for being knocked out of the game (Health 0) or out of gas (Fatigue empty), and it follows the MLB substitution rules above.
must_avoid: Any bar effect that changes, re-rolls, upgrades or reinterprets a play that already happened, or any bar logic that draws from the main play RNG.

Two fatigue systems at once (keeping section 5's falloff alongside the new bar), or a Health bar that drains steadily with workload and barely recovers between innings, which works as a second fatigue meter (Design 2: 57% of starters reach the Health penalty zone).

Fatigue penalties that start well before the real pitch budget (for example at 40% of the tank left, about pitch 54), which changes section 5's 'past the budget' semantics and, once centered, rewards pulling pitchers early.

Health damage multipliers that depend on hidden information or situational flavor ('super effective' x1.5 for a correct guess, 'critical' x1.5 for two-out RBIs). They double-count the guess's outcome effect and have no baseball rationale a fan would accept.
An AI Health hook at Pro that fires before HP 0 (e.g. HP<=35 with runners on), which makes KO faints unreachable (0% in the sim) and the faint mechanic invisible in AI play.
An AI that deliberately rides pitchers into fumes or faints as standard practice (GAS in 25-45% of starts, a faint in 50-75% of games).
Non-injury mid-PA forced changes in AI games, or loose targets like 'mid-PA changes <= 1% of PAs' (about 0.4 per game).
Floating-point bar math (0.9 / 0.2 / 0.4) with exact-equality fixtures or threshold checks.
A drain that averages above 1.0 per pitch while B is labeled in real pitches (Design 3's 1.19, 'Budget 88, red after ~74').
Reliever tanks so small (20-25 units) that the 3-batter minimum plus one long inning routinely forces fumes pitching or out-of-gas faints.
Heals that let a floored or deferred pitcher escape a faint he has already earned (a strikeout lifting him from 1 HP to 3 HP so he stays in).
New ratings built from noisy stats (Poise from LOB%) or bar sizes that vary by role or difficulty in ways that change who pitches while being called 'calibration-safe'.

Injuries that depend on current Health (a comebacker 'injures' only a pitcher who has been shelled), comebacker narration that contradicts the resolved result, graphic injury text, or injuries without a disable flag.

Scope creep in v1: a bullpen warm-up/COLD timer system, modal pinch-hit prompts after every pitching change, Season injury lists and reliever carryover, unless they are separately calibrated and tested.
Uncentered penalties absorbed by quietly fudging base rates, which moves individual real players off their stat lines. Use centering or an A/B check instead.
Worked examples that are impossible or incomplete as baseball sequences (for example '1B, 1B, BB, 2B, 2-run HR') or that state a result without the event script, used as unit fixtures.
Wrong rule citations in the spec or code comments (inherited runners are 9.16(g), the walk charge is 9.16(h), relief ER is 9.16(i)), and tests asserting that the sum of pitcher ER equals team ER.

A saved state that omits pendingForcedChange, faintDeferred, the count at change for 9.16(h), responsible pitcher per runner, or every RNG stream's state, so that a reload during a faint or mid-PA change is ambiguous.
Position players who can faint (cascading position players or deadlocks), or any path where a game cannot terminate.
Sanity-sim numbers presented as evidence when the script's defaults don't reproduce them or the sim uses different coefficients, bullpen size or run environment than the spec.

result.new_section_markdown:
### Pitcher health, fatigue and fainting

It's still baseball. Every pitch and play resolves and is recorded first, by the rules above. A hit is a hit, an out is an out, and runs, outs, innings and the win are pure baseball. The bars only decide how well a pitcher throws from the next pitch on, and when he has to leave. Batters have no bars and never faint. Their bar is the count.

**Health (HP): how hard he's been hit today.** At 0 he's knocked out of the game. It is not a medical bar.
- 100 for every pitcher, every game. No new rating: better pitchers take less damage because they allow less.
- Damage, after the play is final: walk or HBP 4, single 6, double 10, triple 12, home run 16, wild pitch or balk 2.
- Plus 10 for each run that scores while he's on the mound, inherited runners included. A tainted run costs 5: the runner reached on an error or is the extra-inning runner, or he scored on an error or passed ball. Never use official ER here; it can change later in the inning.
- No damage for outs, intentional walks, errors, passed balls or steals. The same scorebook event always costs the same.
- Restores: +8 when a half-inning ends with no run scored while he pitched ("settled in"), +10 for a mound visit. Never above 100.
- Rough math at league rates: an average starter ends around 60–70. About 5 runs on 8 hits in 3 innings knocks him out.

**Fatigue (FTG): his pitch budget.** At 0 he's out of gas. This is section 5's pitch budget made visible, and it is the only fatigue system.
- Budget B: his real pitches per start (SP) or per relief appearance (RP/CL), blended as in section 3, clamped 12–105, set through Stamina. Tank T = max(round(1.3 × B), 30). B 88 gives T 114. B 17 gives T 30.
- Cost per pitch, kept as integer hundredths: 90, +20 with any runner on base, +40 from his 21st pitch of the inning. Tune the base so the league average is 100 ± 2, so B, T and "used" (hundredths ÷ 100) all read as real pitch counts. Intentional walks cost 0.
- Nothing restores it during a game. Dugout time and mound visits don't rest an arm.

**Effects on pitching.** Read once before each pitch, from the bars after the last pitch. They change only the pitcher's inputs, before log5. They never touch a play already made.
- Fatigue: pF = clamp((used − B) / (T − B), 0, 1), so 0 until he passes his budget. In-zone rate × (1 − 0.10 pF), whiff rate × (1 − 0.20 pF), HR allowed × (1 + 0.40 pF), BABIP allowed + .020 pF, wild pitches × (1 + pF). Shown velocity drops 3 mph × pF.
- Health: pH = clamp((40 − HP) / 40, 0, 1), so 0 at 40 or more. In-zone rate × (1 − 0.05 pH), mistake chance (the pitch catches the heart of the plate) + 4 points × pH, wild pitches × (1 + 0.5 pH). Command only: no effect on stuff or velocity.
- Real rates already include tired innings, so center each effect: use (pF − PF_MEAN) and (pH − PH_MEAN), measured in calibration and then frozen. Clamp every probability to 0.02–0.95.

**Fainting.** Either bar at 0 means he faints and is forced out: KO (Health), GAS (Fatigue) or INJ (injury). A destroyed bar always ends in a faint.
- After every pitch, in this order: resolve and record the play; count a finished PA toward his 3-batter total; apply the Fatigue cost and Health damage; roll for a comebacker; check for a faint; if the half ended and he's still in, apply the settled-in heal.
- He leaves at the first legal moment: the end of the current PA or of the half-inning, once the 3-batter minimum is met. Until then the bar holds at 1, he's flagged faintDeferred and he pitches at full penalties ("running on fumes", "hanging on"). No heal cancels it.
- So the AI never changes pitchers mid at-bat. A faint on the 3rd out means he doesn't come back out. A faint on the final out or a walk-off is logged, with no replacement.
- Comebacker: only on a grounder or liner whose result is a single or an infield out. Roll on the aux RNG: 0.07% of those balls strike him, and 20% of those are injuries (INJ), whatever his bars. A pitcher struck but not hurt takes no damage. An injury is immediate and exempt from the 3-batter minimum. Never rolled for a position player.

**Pitching changes follow MLB rules.**
- The reliever enters with full bars and no warm-up penalty (a simplification). An injured pitcher's replacement may take as many warm-ups as he needs (5.07(b)).
- 3-batter minimum (5.10(g)): a pitcher may leave only after 3 finished PAs this appearance (retired or reached base, intentional walks included), at the end of a half, or when injured. Coming back out for a new inning keeps the count going (CONFIG flag; check the current rulebook). Track it separately from his BF stat.
- Mid at-bat change (your BULLPEN only, after the minimum): the reliever inherits the batter, count, runners and outs, and that batter counts toward his minimum. Pitches already thrown stay with the departed pitcher. If the count was 2-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2 and the batter walks, the walk and that runner go to the departed pitcher (9.16(h)). Anything else, a strikeout included, goes to the reliever.
- Inherited runners stay charged to the pitcher who put them on (9.16(g)). If a fielder's choice retires one, the batter-runner takes over that charge. A runner caught stealing or picked off passes nothing on. The reliever's line shows IR/IRS, but his Health still takes the 10. Relievers get no benefit of earlier errors (9.16(i)). The extra-inning runner is unearned, belongs to the pitcher who started the half, and is not a batter faced.
- No re-entry (5.10(d)): a removed pitcher can't come back or move to the field. The engine rejects it and the UI greys him out as FNT or USED. A two-way player who also hits stays in as DH (5.11(b)).
- Empty bullpen, in order: an available pitcher; a tired reliever (Season); a bench position player; the DH to the mound (the DH ends and he keeps his batting spot, 5.11); a fielder to the mound with the DH taking his position. A position player can't faint (bars hold at 1), so every game ends. If nobody is left, the pitcher stays in at 1 and it's logged.
- Position player profile: 70 mph lob fastball and 55 mph eephus; K 6%, BB 10%, HR per batter 7%, BABIP .330. Voluntary use only when trailing by 8+, leading by 10+ in the 6th or later, or in extra innings. Using one at any score when out of pitchers is a house rule.
- Pinch hitters enter only between plate appearances, so 9.15(b) never applies. A starter needs 4.0 IP for the win (house scaling of 9.17(b)'s 5.0, in CONFIG). A fainted pitcher keeps his line and can be the pitcher of record.

**AI manager.** The rules are the same at every difficulty. Only the hooks and the help change. Pro (also used by AUTO and calibration), checked between batters and at the start of each half:
- Start of a half: replace him if used ≥ B − 8.
- Mid-inning: replace him if he's past B with a runner in scoring position, or if 12 or fewer pitches are left in the tank.
- No Health hook: Health 0 is the hook. Visit once when his Health first drops to 30 or below, if a visit is left.
- Matchups and the closer as above.
- Rookie: start-of-half hook at B, mid-inning only at 6 or fewer left, no AI visits. You get coach prompts at Health under 40, at 0.8B and at B ("Smith is tiring. Bring in Jones?"). All-Star: start-of-half hook at B − 14, and AI hitters take 5 points more often on 0-0 and 1-0 against a pitcher past budget.

**Your controls.**
- Both pitchers' bars are always shown. Pitch count, hits, walks and runs are public information.
- BULLPEN lists relievers with throws, role, budget and availability. FNT and USED pitchers are greyed out. During the minimum it's disabled: "Smith must face 2 more batters (3-batter minimum)."

Where things go: the user's gameplay note replaces the section 4 line that said the pitcher's bar is stamina. The full rules are a new subsection at the end of section 5. It is anchored on the box-score line, which no edit touches, so the insert works whether it is applied before or after the edits. I checked all 14 edits in a scratch copy at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-atom/25041982-ed1b-52c3-a1a9-d5a354d2bd12/scratchpad/merge/brief_new.md: each old_str is unique, and both orders give the same file. There are no em dashes and no section is renumbered. The subsection is 68 lines.

What I merged from the three designs:
- From Design 3, the bar mechanics. Health is a flat table keyed only to scorebook events: walk 4, single 6, double 10, triple 12, homer 16, plus 10 per run scored on his watch (5 if tainted). It has no multipliers and never reads official ER. It heals only after a scoreless half (+8) or a visit (+10). Bars change in one write point and are read at one read point. Bar randomness uses its own aux RNG. Effects are centered, with an effects-off/on A/B check.
- From Design 1, the fatigue rules and baseball detail. Fatigue is section 5's pitch budget made visible and replaces the old fatigue path. It is stored in integer hundredths and tuned to a mean of 100 per pitch, so "budget 88" really means 88 pitches. Health affects command only; Fatigue affects everything. Also from Design 1: real box-score notes, visit limits that include the 6th-inning bonus, and Season rules.
- From Design 2, finishing the batter. A non-injury faint waits until the plate appearance ends.

How I settled the disagreements, baseball logic first:
- A destroyed bar always ends in a faint. If he can't leave yet (mid at-bat, or under the 3-batter minimum), the bar holds at 1 with faintDeferred set, and no heal cancels it.
- The AI has no Health hook. A KO is the manager's hook, so knockouts stay visible.
- Comebackers only happen on singles and infield outs. Injury is a fixed 20% share of them, whatever his bars. Because a ball in play always ends the at-bat, the AI makes exactly 0 mid at-bat pitching changes, and only your BULLPEN can produce the inherited-count case.
- The reliever tank has a floor of 30 pitches.
- I dropped warm-up timers and Rushed or Cold statuses, a new Poise rating, and per-out heals.
- I took Season mode in its smallest form: rotation rest, tired relievers sitting out, and injury absences, all with tests.
- Rule citations are corrected: 9.16(g), (h) and (i) are now distinct, and 5.07(b) is used only for injuries.
- The empty-bullpen order is: tired reliever, then bench player, then DH, then a fielder. Position players can't faint, so every game ends.
- Pinch hitters come in only between at-bats, so 9.15(b) never applies.

Open items to check:
- Whether the 3-batter count carries into a new inning. It defaults to carrying over, behind a CONFIG flag, and needs checking against the current rulebook.
- The 4.0 IP starter-win threshold. As written, 9.17(b) requires 5.0 in a game of six innings; 4.0 is a declared house scaling, also in CONFIG.
- Every number is a starting value to calibrate. None of them has been checked against the real engine.
